@code {
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private EditContext _editContext = default!;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private SignInInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? ReturnUrl { get; set; }

    /// <summary>
    /// The registration surface, carrying this page's return URL so the two are interchangeable
    /// entry points to the same destination (§4.4). Not sanitized here — <c>/register</c> passes it
    /// through <see cref="ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl"/> before it redirects anywhere,
    /// exactly as this page does with its own.
    /// </summary>
    private string RegisterUrl => string.IsNullOrEmpty(ReturnUrl)
        ? AccountRoutes.Register
        : $"{AccountRoutes.Register}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(ReturnUrl)}";

    // BL0008: on a static-SSR form POST the framework binds [SupplyParameterFromForm] itself and may
    // assign null, silently discarding a `= new()` initializer — so the default is applied here instead.
    // OnSubmit means we validate by hand (below), so we drive an explicit EditContext.
    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        Input ??= new();
        _editContext = new EditContext(Input);
    }

    private async Task SignInUserAsync()
    {
        string destination = ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl);

        // Passkey path (§3.3): the element posted an assertion credential (or an error). Handle it
        // before any password validation — the username/password fields are irrelevant here — and
        // note PasskeySignInAsync never returns RequiresTwoFactor (a passkey bypasses the §3.5 second
        // factor by construction).
        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Input.Passkey?.Error))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That passkey could not be used. Try again, or sign in with your password.";
            return;
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Input.Passkey?.CredentialJson))
        {
            SignInResult passkeyResult = await SignInManager.PasskeySignInAsync(Input.Passkey.CredentialJson);

            if (passkeyResult.Succeeded)
            {
                Navigation.NavigateTo(destination);
            }
            else if (passkeyResult.IsLockedOut)
            {
                _errorMessage = "Too many failed attempts. The account is locked for about five minutes — try again then.";
            }
            else if (passkeyResult.IsNotAllowed)
            {
                _errorMessage = "This account has been deactivated. Ask at the counter if you think that is a mistake.";
            }
            else
            {
                _errorMessage = "That passkey did not work. Try again, or sign in with your password.";
            }

            return;
        }

        // Password path: OnSubmit fires regardless of validity, so enforce the DataAnnotations now.
        if (!_editContext.Validate())
        {
            return;
        }

        // isPersistent: the §3.1 session is a 24-hour sliding cookie either way; persisting it lets
        // a guest's phone survive a browser restart mid-meal. lockoutOnFailure per §3.1.
        SignInResult result = await SignInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(
            Input.Username,
            Input.Password,
            isPersistent: true,
            lockoutOnFailure: true);

        if (result.Succeeded)
        {
            // The obligations middleware intercepts this navigation when a §3.5 flag is set.
            Navigation.NavigateTo(destination);
        }
        else if (result.RequiresTwoFactor)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(
                $"{AccountRoutes.SignInTwoFactor}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(destination)}");
        }
        else if (result.IsLockedOut)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Too many failed attempts. The account is locked for about five minutes — try again then.";
        }
        else if (result.IsNotAllowed)
        {
            _errorMessage = "This account has been deactivated. Ask at the counter if you think that is a mistake.";
        }
        else
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username and password combination did not work.";
        }
    }

    private sealed class SignInInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter your username.")]
        public string Username { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter your password.")]
        public string Password { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        // Populated by the passkey-submit element on the assertion path; ignored by the password path.
        // Not [Required] — the passkey button must submit without a username or password.
        public PasskeyInputModel? Passkey { get; set; }
    }
}

@*
    Renders the passkey button plus the form-associated <passkey-submit> custom element (passkey.js).

    [Parameter]

    /// <summary>

    /// leaves passkey.js on <see cref="AccountRoutes.PasskeyCreationOptions"/>; the setup wizard sets
    /// it to <see cref="AccountRoutes.SetupPasskeyCreationOptions"/> (§3.6).

    [Parameter]

    /// <summary>
    /// Overrides the request (assertion) options endpoint the element fetches. Null (the default)
    /// leaves passkey.js on <see cref="AccountRoutes.PasskeyRequestOptions"/>. Provided for symmetry;
    /// the setup wizard only registers passkeys, so it does not set this.
    /// </summary>
    [Parameter]

# FILE: src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Layout/AppColophon.razor
################################################################################

--- METADATA ---
  Relative path:         src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Layout/AppColophon.razor
  Size:                  3.4 KiB (3487 bytes)
  SHA-256:               3a22107b16fdf1d7c88c6b6ad593a4156c571499d9fb4d70b2234f9dc45cc66f

--- CONTENT ---
@* The colophon (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.9). One line under the wall clock, on every page, in
   both layouts: what this build is, and a link to the offer of its source.

   WHY IT IS ON EVERY PAGE rather than tucked into an "about" nobody visits. AGPL-3.0-only §13 says a
   modified version "must prominently offer all users interacting with it remotely through a computer
   network ... an opportunity to receive the Corresponding Source". This application is published so
   that other people will run it, and CONTRIBUTING.md tells them their fork "owes its users the same"
   — so the mechanism that discharges that obligation belongs in the program, set by one environment
   variable, rather than left as a page each operator has to remember to write. A footer link on every
   page is the customary reading of "prominently"; a link only a signed-in administrator can reach is
   not an offer to all users, which is also why §3.5's obligations pipeline exempts the destination.

   Note that the obligation binds whoever *modifies* the Program. An unmodified deployment of this
   tree is not obliged to offer anything. Shipping the offer anyway costs one line and means the
   operator who does modify it complies by changing RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL to point at their fork,
   instead of discovering the requirement afterwards. There is deliberately no switch to turn this
   off: an offer with an off switch is not one, and an operator who genuinely wants it gone has the
   source and the freedom to remove it — which is the whole arrangement.

   WHY THE VERSION IS SHOWN. Two reasons, one operational and one legal. Operationally, "which build
   is this box running?" had no answer obtainable from the running instance before this. Legally, §13
   offers the Corresponding Source "of your version", and an offer that cannot name the revision is
   approximate. The usual objection — that a version number tells an attacker which advisories to try
   — does not survive contact with this project: the source is public, the tags are public, and the
   image digests are public, so concealing the number here would protect nothing and break the offer.

   No @rendermode: static SSR, like the layouts that host it. Nothing here changes after the first
   paint, and a colophon that needed a circuit would be missing from exactly the surfaces that most
   need to state what they are — a sign-in page, a paired tablet, a page rendered before a circuit has
   started. *@

<p class="app-colophon">
    <span class="app-colophon-name">MyRestaurant</span>
    <span class="app-colophon-version" title="@_informationalVersion">@_display</span>
    <a class="app-colophon-link" href="@SourceRoutes.Source">Source code (AGPL-3.0-only)</a>
</p>

@code {
    private string _display = string.Empty;
    private string _informationalVersion = string.Empty;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        // Read once from the static rather than re-derived per render: it cannot change while the
        // process lives, and the reflection behind it should not run on every page of every request.
        BuildInformation build = BuildInformation.Current;
        _display = build.Display;

        // The title attribute carries the unabbreviated stamp, so an operator reading a screenshot
        // over somebody's shoulder can get the full revision without opening the page it links to.
        _informationalVersion = build.InformationalVersion;
    }
}

# FILE: src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Layout/RestaurantClockFooter.razor
################################################################################

--- METADATA ---
  Relative path:         src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Layout/RestaurantClockFooter.razor

@using System.Globalization
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Time
@inject IClock Clock
@inject RestaurantTime RestaurantClock

@* The restaurant wall clock (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.7). On every page, in both layouts.

   Every instant this application shows is rendered in RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE and never in the reader's
   own zone (§8.1) — which is the right rule and an invisible one. A guest reading "sent 3:04 PM" from
   another continent has no way to know whose three o'clock that is unless the page says so, standing
   somewhere they will look. This footer is that statement, and it earns its place by also being useful
   to the people in the building: one authoritative clock, the same on the counter's screen, the
   kitchen's, and the tablet on table four.

   TICKING WITHOUT A TIMER. There is deliberately no server-side timer here. A Blazor timer would tick
   only on interactive pages (half the surfaces here are static SSR), would cost one render and one
   circuit message per second per open tab, and would keep a phone's radio awake to do it. Instead the
   component renders one anchor — the instant, the zone offset that applies to it, and when that offset
   next changes — and js/clock.js advances it locally against a monotonic clock, pausing entirely while
   the tab is hidden. The server is asked again on a page load, and thereafter only rarely (§11.7).

   ShouldRender is pinned false for the same reason: once the anchor is in the DOM the script owns that
   text node, and a re-render from the framework would fight it. Nothing about this component depends on
   state that changes, so there is nothing to lose by never rendering twice. *@

<footer class="app-footer">
    <p class="restaurant-clock"
       id="@ElementId"
       data-epoch-milliseconds="@_epochMilliseconds"
       data-utc-offset-minutes="@_utcOffsetMinutes"
       data-next-transition-epoch-milliseconds="@_nextTransitionEpochMilliseconds"
       data-next-utc-offset-minutes="@_nextUtcOffsetMinutes"
       data-twelve-hour-clock="@_twelveHourClock"
       data-snapshot-url="@RestaurantClockRoutes.Snapshot">
        <span class="restaurant-clock-label">Restaurant time</span>
        <time class="restaurant-clock-reading"
              data-restaurant-clock-reading="true"
              datetime="@_machineReadable">@_reading</time>
        <span class="restaurant-clock-zone" title="@_zoneIdentifier">@_zoneLabel</span>
    </p>
</footer>

@code {
    /// <summary>The element js/clock.js looks for. Exactly one per document.</summary>
    public const string ElementId = "restaurant-clock";

    private string _epochMilliseconds = string.Empty;
    private string _utcOffsetMinutes = string.Empty;
    private string _nextTransitionEpochMilliseconds = string.Empty;
    private string _nextUtcOffsetMinutes = string.Empty;
    private string _twelveHourClock = "true";
    private string _machineReadable = string.Empty;
    private string _reading = string.Empty;
    private string _zoneLabel = string.Empty;
    private string _zoneIdentifier = string.Empty;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        // One instant for the whole component, so the rendered text and the anchor the script starts
        // from cannot disagree by the microseconds between two reads of the clock.
        DateTimeOffset now = Clock.UtcNow;
        RestaurantClockSnapshot snapshot = RestaurantClock.Snapshot(now);

        // Every attribute is formatted invariantly rather than left to the ambient culture: these are
        // numbers a script parses, not text a person reads, and a culture that groups digits or writes
        // a different minus sign would hand js/clock.js something it cannot parse.
        _epochMilliseconds = snapshot.EpochMilliseconds.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        _utcOffsetMinutes = snapshot.UtcOffsetMinutes.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        _nextTransitionEpochMilliseconds =
            snapshot.NextTransitionEpochMilliseconds?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? string.Empty;
        _nextUtcOffsetMinutes =
            snapshot.NextUtcOffsetMinutes?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? string.Empty;
        _twelveHourClock = snapshot.UsesTwelveHourClock ? "true" : "false";

        _reading = RestaurantClock.DateAndTimeWithSeconds(now);
        _machineReadable = RestaurantClock.MachineReadable(now);
        _zoneLabel = snapshot.ZoneLabel;
        _zoneIdentifier = snapshot.ZoneIdentifier;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Never re-render. The script owns this subtree after the first paint; a framework re-render would
    /// overwrite a correct ticking reading with a stale one and reset the script's anchor for nothing.
    /// </summary>
    protected override bool ShouldRender() => false;
}

namespace MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Components.Pages.Administration;

/// <summary>
/// Which of §11.4's administration surfaces a page is, so <c>AdministrationAreaLinks</c> can mark it as
/// the current one (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.4, §11.12).
///
/// <para><b>Why this is an enum and not a string.</b> The six links were copy-pasted into six pages, and
/// each copy omitted a different one — its own — so the row of links was a different row on every page
/// and no page could be reached from every other. An enum means the set is declared once and a page
/// declares only which member it is; a page that forgets loses its highlight and keeps its links, which
/// is the failure worth having.</para>
///
/// <para><b>Why a page links to itself.</b> The self-link is rendered and marked
/// <c>aria-current="page"</c> rather than omitted, so the row reads identically wherever an operator
/// lands and its geography is learnable — on a handset it is a horizontally scrolled strip, where a row
/// whose contents shift between pages cannot be navigated from memory at all.</para>
///
/// <para>Members are ordered as the row renders, which is the order §11.4 lists the sections in.</para>
/// </summary>
public enum AdministrationArea
{
    /// <summary><c>/administration</c> — accounts, roles, credential resets (§3.7).</summary>
    People,

    /// <summary><c>/administration/tables</c> — tables, join secrets, display devices (§4).</summary>
    Tables,

    /// <summary><c>/administration/menu</c> — menu sections and items, and their event history (§7).</summary>
    Menu,

    /// <summary><c>/administration/sittings</c> — open sittings, end-of-day close, corrections (§5.4, §6.7).</summary>
    Sittings,

    /// <summary><c>/administration/hidden-records</c> — every hidden order system-wide (§6.8).</summary>
    HiddenRecords,

    /// <summary><c>/administration/events</c> — the security, order and menu event explorer (§11.4).</summary>
    Events,

@page "/administration/menu"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]

@* The administration menu index (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §7, §11.4, §11.12 — `area.administration`:
   "Menu (CRUD + activity, event history per item)"). It lists every HEADING with the items filed
   under it, links each of both to its own management page, offers creation of either, and shows the
   recent activity feed that answers "what changed today" without opening an item.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. Deactivated items are listed, not filtered: §7 is
   explicit that an 86'd item stays on the menu marked "currently unavailable", and a page that hid
   them from the administrator would hide exactly the rows somebody is looking for. The same holds one
   register up, and more strongly: an inactive SECTION is hidden from the guest entirely and from
   §11.4's administrator not at all — whose job on this page may be stocking next week's breakfast
   menu before switching it on.

   **THIS IS SECTIONS-FIRST AS OF M6 SLICE 44, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE SURFACE.** Until now it
   was a flat list of every item with the heading as a COLUMN, which is what a menu index looks like
   when the model has just learned to express a menu and the surface has not caught up. Slice 40 shipped
   the column as the honest intermediate and said so: a record list whose rows link nowhere is a list of
   dead ends, so the fact went on the screen and the destination waited for the editor it had to open
   into. The editor landed in Slice 41 and the refile verb in Slice 43. This is the destination.

   **A heading is a `<details>` rendered open, and the item list inside it is §11.12's record list.**
   The disclosure is native: no script on a page that hosts no island, a real disclosure in the
   accessibility tree rather than a div somebody wired up, and no state on the server. It is rendered
   open on every request because a heading collapsed by the server is a heading whose items nobody
   looking for an item can find — and because §16.3 scenario 16 measures what the layout engine laid
   out, so a closed group would quietly remove its own controls from the barrier that exists to find
   exactly that. Collapsing is the operator's decision, not this page's.

   **AN EMPTY HEADING IS VISIBLE HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME.** The list this page used to render was built
   from ITEMS, so a heading with nothing under it appeared nowhere on it — the old code said so in a
   comment beside a count that meant "sections that have something in them". A heading created with a
   typo, or one stocked for next week and not yet filled, was a row this surface could not show. It now
   reads both lists and renders the headings, so emptiness is a state with a sentence rather than an
   absence.

   **THIS PAGE CAN NOW REORDER A HEADING, AND THAT IS WHAT SLICE 47 IS.** For three slices the cut was
   recorded here rather than papered over: `ReorderMenuSectionAsync` sets an ABSOLUTE `display_order`,
   and positions are deliberately non-unique with a name tiebreak (§7), so "move this heading up" is not
   expressible as one absolute write — two headings sharing a position have an order nobody assigned and
   no single number distinguishes them. The verb that expresses it is `ResequenceMenuSectionsAsync`,
   which takes the WHOLE ordering and assigns 0…n-1 from it, and this page is its only caller: the list
   below is already rendered in stored order, so Up and Down exchange two entries in that list and post
   all of it. Nothing is computed from a position, which is the point — a number that means "one less
   than the heading above" cannot be written when two headings share a number.

   Each button is its own form with its own `@@formname`, because Blazor's static SSR dispatches a POST
   to the form that names it and there is one pair per heading. The first heading's Up and the last
   heading's Down are rendered DISABLED rather than omitted: a control that vanishes at the edge of a
   list moves every other control up a row on the render after a move, and §16.3 scenario 16 measures
   where controls are.

   An absolute position is still writable, on the heading's own page, and that is not a duplicate:
   somebody who wants breakfast at 0 and does not care what else moves is stating an absolute, and the
   editor's number field is where that belongs.

   Two record lists (§11.12) and no inline <style>. The group vocabulary is `.menu-group*` in app.css. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// Enough to cover a service's worth of 86s without turning the index into the archive. §11.4's
    /// "filters narrow only on explicit request" governs the per-item history, which is uncapped; this
    /// panel is a glance, and its cap is the explicit request.
    /// </summary>
    private const int RecentActivityCount = 20;

    private IReadOnlyList<MenuSectionSummary>? _sections;
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _items = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemEventEntry>? _recent;
    private int _itemCount;
    private int _activeItemCount;
    private int _describedItemCount;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // Two reads rather than one, and the second is the one this surface gained. IMenuDirectory
        // builds its list from menu_item, so a heading with nothing under it is not in it at all —
        // which is precisely the row an administrator wondering where their new heading went is looking
        // for. IMenuSectionDirectory is the list of headings themselves, empty ones included, and its
        // own doc comment says that is what it is for.
        _sections = await MenuSections.ListAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        _items = await MenuItems.ListAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        _itemCount = _items.Count;
        _activeItemCount = _items.Count(item => item.IsActive);
        _describedItemCount = _items.Count(item => item.Description.Length > 0);

        _recent = await MenuEvents.ListRecentAsync(RecentActivityCount, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Post/redirect/get, the shape every administration write on this tree uses: a committed move
        // redirects back here with one word, so a refresh cannot re-post it. On a POST the handler below
        // is about to run and there is nothing to say yet.
        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Exchanges one heading with its neighbour and posts the <b>whole</b> ordering (§7).
    ///
    /// <para><b>The list is the source of the move, which is why this takes an offset rather than a
    /// position.</b> <c>_sections</c> is what the page rendered, in the order §7's read produced; the
    /// exchange happens in a copy of it and the result is sent as the complete ordering. So the write is
    /// expressible even when two headings share a <c>display_order</c> — which the schema permits on
    /// purpose, and which is the whole reason an absolute write could not express it.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><b>Every failure here is a stale page rather than a fault, and each reloads.</b> An identifier
    /// this render does not hold, or a neighbour past either end, means somebody else changed the menu
    /// between this page being drawn and the button being pressed. The same is true of
    /// <c>MenuSectionSetChanged</c>, which the write service returns when the ordering is no longer a
    /// permutation of the stored set — it refuses rather than reconciling, and the honest answer on this
    /// side is to render the truth again.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private async Task MoveAsync(Guid menuSectionIdentifier, int offset)
    {
        if (_sections is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(IndexPath);
            return;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees this; menu_section_event.actor_person_identifier
            // is NOT NULL and §7 requires every change to name somebody, so this is the belt to that brace
            // — the same helper ManageMenuSection carries, in the one form this page needs.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        List<Guid> ordering = _sections.Select(summary => summary.MenuSectionIdentifier).ToList();

        int from = ordering.IndexOf(menuSectionIdentifier);
        int to = from + offset;

        if (from < 0 || to < 0 || to >= ordering.Count)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(IndexPath);
            return;
        }

        (ordering[from], ordering[to]) = (ordering[to], ordering[from]);

        ResequenceMenuSectionsOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.ResequenceMenuSectionsAsync(
            ordering, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case ResequenceMenuSectionsOutcome.Resequenced:
                RedirectWithOutcome("moved");
                break;
            case ResequenceMenuSectionsOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("move-no-change");
                break;
            case ResequenceMenuSectionsOutcome.MenuSectionSetChanged:
                RedirectWithOutcome("menu-changed");
                break;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The items filed under one heading, in the order guests read them.
    ///
    /// <para><b>Filtered rather than grouped, and rather than asked for per section.</b> §7's read
    /// orders by <c>(section.display_order, section.name, section.menu_section_identifier,
    /// item.display_order, item.name, item.menu_item_identifier)</c>, so this filter preserves the order
    /// somebody chose without re-deciding it — where a <c>GroupBy</c> would re-order the headings into
    /// hash order and make the ordering decision a second time in a second file. A per-section read
    /// would be a query with one caller, which is the defect <see cref="IMenuDirectory"/> declines to
    /// invent for exactly this reason. The menu is single-digit-to-sixty rows on the machine this runs
    /// on, and the same filter is what <c>ManageMenuSection</c> already does.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> ItemsUnder(MenuSectionSummary section)
        => _items.Where(item => item.MenuSectionIdentifier == section.MenuSectionIdentifier).ToArray();

    /// <summary>
    /// How many items are under a heading, as a phrase rather than a bare number, because it sits in a
    /// summary line beside a position and two adjacent integers with no words between them are
    /// unreadable.
    /// </summary>
    private string ItemCountLabel(MenuSectionSummary section)
    {
        int count = ItemsUnder(section).Count;

        return count switch
        {
            0 => "no items",
            1 => "1 item",
            _ => $"{count} items",
        };
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether a heading is at an end of the list, which is what disables one of its two buttons. Compared
    /// by identifier rather than by <c>display_order</c>, and that is the same distinction the whole verb
    /// rests on: two headings may share a position, so "has the lowest number" is not "is first" — but
    /// "is the first entry of the list this page is rendering" is exactly what Up would exchange with
    /// nothing.
    /// </summary>
    private bool IsFirst(MenuSectionSummary menuSectionSummary)
        => _sections is null
            || _sections.Count == 0
            || _sections[0].MenuSectionIdentifier == menuSectionSummary.MenuSectionIdentifier;

    private bool IsLast(MenuSectionSummary menuSectionSummary)
        => _sections is null
            || _sections.Count == 0
            || _sections[^1].MenuSectionIdentifier == menuSectionSummary.MenuSectionIdentifier;

    /// <summary>
    /// One form name per heading per direction. Unique within the page because the identifier is, which is
    /// what Blazor's static SSR needs to route a POST to the right handler; a shared name would dispatch
    /// every group's button to whichever form rendered first.
    /// </summary>
    private static string MoveFormName(MenuSectionSummary menuSectionSummary, bool up)
        => $"menu-section-move-{(up ? "up" : "down")}-{menuSectionSummary.MenuSectionIdentifier}";

    private static string IndexPath => "/administration/menu";

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{IndexPath}?done={outcome}");

    /// <summary>
    /// The word the redirect carried, as a sentence. Three outcomes and three sentences, because the two
    /// that wrote nothing are ordinary events on a shared menu rather than errors: somebody else moved the
    /// heading first, or somebody else changed which headings there are.
    /// </summary>
    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "moved" => "Moved. Every open menu has already picked up the new order.",
        "move-no-change" => "It was already in that position — nothing changed.",
        "menu-changed" => "The headings changed while this page was open, so nothing was moved. This is"
            + " the current order; try again.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private static string ManagePath(Guid menuItemIdentifier)
        => $"/administration/menu/{menuItemIdentifier}";

    private static string SectionPath(Guid menuSectionIdentifier)
        => $"/administration/menu/sections/{menuSectionIdentifier}";

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for each event type §8.2's <c>menu_item_event</c> vocabulary CHECK admits,
    /// falling back to the stored string for anything else — §11.4 renders the record, so an
    /// unrecognised type must show as itself rather than be swallowed. The arms below are deliberately
    /// not counted in prose: this comment said <em>five</em> and named <em>two</em> new types where the
    /// plan specified three, in a sentence nothing in the tree could check (F-77).
    ///
    /// <para>This feed is a glance rather than an audit, so a <c>description_changed</c> says that a
    /// description moved without quoting it — the sentence belongs on the item's own page, where the
    /// uncapped history renders it in full.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string Describe(MenuItemEventEntry entry) => entry.EventType switch
    {
        "created" => $"Created at {Money(entry.NewPriceAmount ?? 0m)}",
        "name_changed" => $"Renamed to {entry.NewName}",
        "price_changed" => $"Repriced to {Money(entry.NewPriceAmount ?? 0m)}",
        "description_changed" => (entry.NewDescription ?? string.Empty).Length == 0
            ? "Description cleared"
            : "Description changed",
        "section_changed" => $"Filed under {entry.NewMenuSectionName}",
        "reordered" => $"Moved to position {entry.NewDisplayOrder}",
        "activated" => "Marked available",
        "deactivated" => "Marked unavailable",
        _ => entry.EventType,
    };
}

@* Administration sittings (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §5.4, §11.4, §11.12 — "Sittings (open + recent,
   end-of-day batch close, post-close corrective actions per §6.7)"). Two lists and one button.

   §5.4 is one sentence: "Administration provides batch close: list open sittings with last-activity
   timestamps, select, close each via the same §5.3 transaction." The last-activity column is why the
   page exists — a table whose last event was four hours ago is a table that has gone home, and it is the
   only signal in the system that distinguishes it from a table still eating.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. Nothing is ticked by default and there is no select-all:
   closing twelve tables costs twelve deliberate ticks, and that is the confirmation step rather than a
   second page. This is the one form in the tree that reads its own POST values instead of binding a
   [SupplyParameterFromForm] model — a checkbox per row over a list whose length is however many tables
   are open has no static model to bind to, and the alternative (a select-one picker, as on ManageTable
   and TableDisplays) is not what §5.4 describes.

   The counter reaches the same §5.3 transaction from /counter, one table at a time, with a guest standing
   in front of it. This is the deliberate end-of-service pass over what is left.

   Two shared §11.12 record lists and no inline <style>. The tick is the FIRST thing in each card and
   carries the table's label as its visible text — on a handset a bare checkbox at the top of a card is a
   control with nothing saying what it closes, and this is the one control on an administration index that
   charges somebody money. Its 2.75rem row height is the §11.12 minimum rather than this page's own
   opinion, which is what the old inline `.sittings-tick input { width: 1.35rem }` was. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// The one POST field this page reads. Every checkbox shares it, so the browser posts one value per
    /// ticked row — the standard HTML idiom for "which of these". It must not collide with Blazor's own
    /// reserved <c>_handler</c> field, and it does not.
    /// </summary>
    private const string SelectedSittingField = "sitting";

    /// <summary>
    /// How far back the settled list looks, and how many rows it will draw. Both bounded on purpose:
    /// §11.4 gives administration the complete record <em>per sitting</em>, not an unbounded index of
    /// every sitting the restaurant has ever had. This list answers "what did we settle today".
    /// </summary>
    private const int RecentWindowDays = 7;

    private const int RecentCap = 60;

    private IReadOnlyList<CounterSittingSummary>? _open;
    private IReadOnlyList<CounterSittingSummary>? _closed;
    private int _pendingAcrossOpenSittings;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private int? Closed { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private int? Already { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private int? Missing { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        await LoadAsync();

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Closed, Already, Missing);
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        _open = await CounterReads.ListOpenSittingsAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        _pendingAcrossOpenSittings = _open.Sum(sitting => sitting.PendingLineCount);

        _closed = await CounterReads.ListRecentlyClosedSittingsAsync(
            Clock.UtcNow.AddDays(-RecentWindowDays),
            RecentCap,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §5.4's batch close. The chosen identifiers come from the posted form rather than from a bound
    /// model, because the set of rows is whatever is open right now.
    ///
    /// <para><c>ReadFormAsync</c> is not a second read of the request body: the Blazor endpoint has
    /// already parsed the form to find which handler to invoke, and <c>HttpRequest</c> caches the parsed
    /// collection, so this returns the same instance the framework used. Awaiting the cached path rather
    /// than touching <c>Request.Form</c> synchronously keeps the cancellation token honoured.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private async Task CloseSelectedAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that brace,
            // because table_sitting.closed_by_person_identifier is NOT NULL whenever closed_at is set and
            // has no anonymous option.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        IFormCollection form = await HttpContext.Request.ReadFormAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        List<Guid> chosen = [];
        foreach (string? posted in form[SelectedSittingField])
        {
            // A value that will not parse is discarded rather than reported: the only way to post one is
            // to hand-edit the form, and the honest answer to "close sitting 'banana'" is that no such
            // sitting was closed, which the counts already say.
            if (Guid.TryParse(posted, out Guid sittingIdentifier))
            {
                chosen.Add(sittingIdentifier);
            }
        }

        if (chosen.Count == 0)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Nothing was ticked, so nothing was closed. Tick the tables that have finished.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        EndOfDayResult result = await Settlement.CloseManyAsync(
            chosen, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Post/redirect/get, so a refresh does not re-post a close. The counts travel in the query string;
        // the money does not, because the settled list below re-renders from the database and shows every
        // stamped total in the restaurant's own currency rather than one reconstructed from a URL.
        Navigation.NavigateTo(
            $"/administration/sittings?closed={result.ClosedCount}" +
            $"&already={result.AlreadyClosedCount}" +
            $"&missing={result.NotFoundCount}");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The sentence after a redirect. Three numbers because three things can happen to a ticked table:
    /// it closed, somebody had already closed it, or it is not there any more. The second is not a
    /// failure — a counter settling a table while an administrator was reading this page is the system
    /// working — so it is reported as fact rather than as a warning.
    /// </summary>
    private static string? FlashFor(int? closed, int? already, int? missing)
    {
        if (closed is null && already is null && missing is null)
        {
            return null;
        }

        int closedCount = closed ?? 0;
        int alreadyCount = already ?? 0;
        int missingCount = missing ?? 0;

        List<string> parts = [];

        parts.Add(closedCount == 1
            ? "Settled 1 sitting."
            : $"Settled {closedCount} sittings.");

        if (alreadyCount > 0)
        {
            parts.Add(alreadyCount == 1
                ? "1 had already been settled at the counter — nothing changed on it."
                : $"{alreadyCount} had already been settled at the counter — nothing changed on those.");
        }

        if (missingCount > 0)
        {
            parts.Add(missingCount == 1
                ? "1 no longer exists."
                : $"{missingCount} no longer exist.");
        }

        return string.Join(" ", parts);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// How long ago, in words, so the last-activity column can be read at a glance. Deliberately coarse:
    /// the question §5.4 is asking is "has this table gone home", and the exact instant is in the cell
    /// beside it.
    /// </summary>
    private string AgeOf(DateTimeOffset instant)
    {
        TimeSpan elapsed = Clock.UtcNow - instant;

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.Zero)
        {
            // Only reachable if the database clock is ahead of this process's. Say nothing rather than
            // "-3 minutes ago".
            return string.Empty;
        }

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1))
        {
            return "just now";
        }

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.FromHours(1))
        {
            int minutes = (int)elapsed.TotalMinutes;
            return $"{minutes} {(minutes == 1 ? "minute" : "minutes")} ago";
        }

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.FromDays(1))
        {
            int hours = (int)elapsed.TotalHours;
            return $"{hours} {(hours == 1 ? "hour" : "hours")} ago";
        }

        int days = (int)elapsed.TotalDays;
        return $"{days} {(days == 1 ? "day" : "days")} ago";
    }

    private static string CheckboxId(CounterSittingSummary sitting)
        => $"close-{sitting.SittingIdentifier}";

    private static string RecordPath(CounterSittingSummary sitting)
        => $"/administration/sittings/{sitting.SittingIdentifier}";

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);
}

@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]

@* Create a menu item (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §7, §11.4). Administrator only (endpoint authorization,

@code {
    private CreateMenuItemResult? _created;
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuSectionSummary>? _sections;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "create-menu-item")]
    private CreateMenuItemInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        Input ??= new();

        _sections = await MenuSections.ListAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Pre-selected rather than left on Guid.Empty. A <select> with no selected option shows its
        // first one and posts that value, so a form that left this at the default would LOOK correct
        // and submit an identifier naming nothing — which the write service would report and the person
        // would read as a bug. Only on the first render: a re-render after a failed post must keep what
        // was chosen.
        if (Input.MenuSectionIdentifier == Guid.Empty && _sections.Count > 0)
        {
            Input.MenuSectionIdentifier = _sections[0].MenuSectionIdentifier;
        }
    }

    private async Task CreateAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that
            // brace, because menu_item_event.actor_person_identifier is NOT NULL and §7 requires every
            // change to name somebody.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        _created = await MenuChanges.CreateMenuItemAsync(
            IdentifierFactory.Create(),
            Input.MenuSectionIdentifier,
            Input.Name.Trim(),
            Input.Description,
            Input.PriceAmount,
            administrator,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // A section deleted or renamed out from under a form somebody left open. Reported rather than
        // thrown: the outcome exists precisely so this page can say which field was wrong instead of
        // showing a foreign-key constraint name.
        if (_created.Outcome is CreateMenuItemOutcome.MenuSectionNotFound)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                "That section no longer exists. It may have been changed while this page was open —"
                + " reload the page and choose again.";
        }
    }

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    private sealed class CreateMenuItemInputModel
    {
        // No [Required] attribute, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: Guid is a value type,
        // so [Required] passes on Guid.Empty and would assert nothing. The select is pre-selected, has
        // no empty option, and the write service reports an identifier that names nothing — three
        // defences, none of which is a validation attribute that does not work.
        public Guid MenuSectionIdentifier { get; set; }

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Give the item a name.")]
        [StringLength(120, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The name must be 1–120 characters.")]
        public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        // No [Required]: §7 makes a description optional and a blank one is stored as "". The 2,000 is
        // this form's own limit rather than the column's — `menu_item.description` is `text` and has none
        // — and it is here rather than in DapperMenuAdministration for the reason that file records: a
        // ceiling invented in the data-access layer would be that layer overruling the schema of record.
        // A form is allowed an opinion about how much prose fits on a menu.
        [StringLength(2000, ErrorMessage = "The description must be 2,000 characters or fewer.")]
        public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        // The upper bound is numeric(10,2)'s: eight digits before the point. Bounded here so the form
        // says so, and again in DapperMenuAdministration so no other caller can get past it.
        [Range(0, 99999999.99, ErrorMessage = "The price must be between 0 and 99,999,999.99.")]
        public decimal PriceAmount { get; set; }
    }
}

    private string? _errorMessage;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "create-menu-section")]
    private CreateMenuSectionInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        => Input ??= new();

    private async Task CreateAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that
            // brace, because menu_section_event.actor_person_identifier is NOT NULL and §7 requires
            // every change to name somebody.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        _created = await MenuChanges.CreateMenuSectionAsync(
            IdentifierFactory.Create(),
            Input.Name.Trim(),
            Input.Description,
            administrator,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // The collision is reported rather than thrown, because it is a mis-tap and not a fault: the
        // UNIQUE constraint on a citext column is what catches a second "Drinks", and the person who
        // typed it needs to be told which of the two words was the problem.
        if (_created.Outcome is CreateMenuSectionOutcome.NameTaken)
        {
            _errorMessage =

        }

    private sealed class CreateMenuSectionInputModel
    {
        // The 80 is the column's own ceiling this time rather than a form's opinion:
        // menu_section.name is CHECK (char_length BETWEEN 1 AND 80), so a longer name would be
        // PostgreSQL error 23514 well after the form that caused it. menu_item.name has no such
        // constraint, which is why CreateMenuItem's limit is 120 and is that form's own choice.
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Give the section a name.")]
        [StringLength(80, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The name must be 1–80 characters.")]
        public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        // this form's own limit rather than the column's — menu_section.description is `text` and has
        // none — and it matches CreateMenuItem's for the same reason that one gives.

        public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

@code {
    private bool _created;
    private string? _createdUsername;
    private Guid _createdPersonIdentifier;
    private string? _temporaryPassword;
    private string? _grantedRolesText;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "create-staff")]
    private CreateStaffInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        => Input ??= new();

    private async Task CreateAsync()
    {
        Person? actingAdministrator = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (actingAdministrator is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        string username = Input.Username.Trim();
        string? displayName = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Input.DisplayName) ? null : Input.DisplayName.Trim();

        // Best-effort duplicate check; the person UNIQUE constraint inside the transaction is authoritative.
        if (await UserManager.FindByNameAsync(username) is not null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username is already taken. Please choose another.";
            return;
        }

        List<string> roles = [];
        if (Input.GrantAdministrator)
        {
            roles.Add(RestaurantRoles.Administrator);
        }

        if (Input.GrantCounter)
        {
            roles.Add(RestaurantRoles.Counter);
        }

        if (Input.GrantKitchen)
        {
            roles.Add(RestaurantRoles.Kitchen);
        }

        Guid personIdentifier = IdentifierFactory.Create();

        // A generated temporary password, hashed immediately so the plaintext is only ever held for the
        // one response that shows it. 12 random bytes render to a 16-character URL-safe string — well
        // over the 12-character policy floor (§3.2), which the forced change re-checks anyway.
        string temporaryPassword = SecretGenerator.GenerateBase64UrlSecret(12);
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = personIdentifier, Username = username },
            temporaryPassword);

        CreateStaffStatus status = await Accounts.CreateStaffAsync(
            new NewStaffAccount(personIdentifier, username, displayName, passwordHash, roles),
            actingAdministrator.PersonIdentifier,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (status == CreateStaffStatus.UsernameTaken)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username was taken while you were filling this in. Please choose another.";
            return;
        }

        _createdUsername = username;
        _createdPersonIdentifier = personIdentifier;
        _temporaryPassword = temporaryPassword;
        _grantedRolesText = FormatRoles(roles);
        _created = true;
    }

    private static string? FormatRoles(IReadOnlyList<string> roles) => roles.Count switch
    {
        0 => null,
        1 => roles[0],
        _ => $"{string.Join(", ", roles.Take(roles.Count - 1))} and {roles[^1]}",
    };

    private sealed class CreateStaffInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a username.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 3, ErrorMessage = "The username must be 3–64 characters.")]
        public string Username { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [StringLength(120, ErrorMessage = "That display name is too long.")]
        public string? DisplayName { get; set; }

        public bool GrantAdministrator { get; set; }

        public bool GrantCounter { get; set; }

        public bool GrantKitchen { get; set; }
    }
}

@code {
    private bool _created;
    private string? _createdLabel;
    private Guid _createdTableIdentifier;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "create-table")]
    private CreateTableInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        => Input ??= new();

    private async Task CreateAsync()
    {
        string label = Input.Label.Trim();
        Guid tableIdentifier = IdentifierFactory.Create();

        CreateTableOutcome outcome = await Tables.CreateTableAsync(
            tableIdentifier, label, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case CreateTableOutcome.Created:
                _createdLabel = label;
                _createdTableIdentifier = tableIdentifier;
                _created = true;
                break;
            case CreateTableOutcome.LabelTaken:
                _errorMessage = "That label is already used by another table. Please choose a different one.";
                break;
        }
    }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    private sealed class CreateTableInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a label for the table.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The label must be 1–64 characters.")]
        public string Label { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@* The event explorer (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.4).

   §11.4's list of administration sections ends with it, in these words: "Event explorer (filter
   security/order/menu events by subject, actor, type, and time)". It is the last thing M5 owes, and the
   only screen in the system that reads across subsystems: every other page answers a question about one
   account, one table, one sitting, or one item, and this one answers "what happened".

   Read-only, and deliberately so. There is no control on this page that changes anything — no unhide, no
   close, no reset. Every row links to the screen that owns the thing it is about, and that screen has
   the buttons. An audit log with edit affordances on it is a different and much worse object.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. The filter is a plain GET form, because a filter is a
   bookmarkable question rather than a mutation: no antiforgery token, no handler, no POST, and every
   narrowing affordance on a row is an ordinary link that works with no JavaScript. The parsing and the
   URL-building live in EventExplorerQuery rather than here, which is what lets both be tested without a
   browser or a container — the thing HiddenRecords' identical inline logic cannot be.

   §11.12, Stage 1b: the page head and the filter are the shared vocabulary now (`.page-head`,
   `AdministrationAreaLinks`, `.filter-form`, `.filter-actions` — all in app.css), and the five
   hand-rolled area links that used to sit in a `.admin-header-actions` div are gone. This page was one
   of the last two carrying that copy: each of the six copies omitted its own page, so the row was a
   different row on every screen and no page was reachable from every other. The `.event-*` rules that
   remain are read by this page alone — a badge palette and an event row — which is what an inline
   <style> is for here. It contains no media query, and cannot: §11.12's one breakpoint is a rule about
   the tree rather than about app.css, and for a slice it was asserted only about app.css (F-63).

   §6.8's order_visibility_event is deliberately not a fourth stream: §11.4 names three, and gives
   visibility its own screen at /administration/hidden-records, where its log sits beside the order it is
   about and next to the Unhide button that is its only counterpart. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How many events the list will draw. §11.4's rule is that administration sees everything and
    /// narrows "only on explicit request", so this is a rendering bound rather than a filter: when it is
    /// reached the page says so and points at the filter, instead of quietly answering a smaller
    /// question. Larger than the hidden-records cap because these three logs are the busiest tables in
    /// the database and a day's worth of one service can pass a hundred rows before lunch.
    /// </summary>
    private const int ListCap = 200;

    private EventExplorerQuery _query = default!;
    private IReadOnlyList<ExplorerEvent>? _events;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.StreamField)]
    private string[]? Streams { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.SubjectField)]
    private string? Subject { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.ActorField)]
    private string? Actor { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.TypeField)]
    private string? EventTypeChoice { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.FromField)]
    private string? From { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.ToField)]
    private string? To { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _query = EventExplorerQuery.Parse(
            Streams, Subject, Actor, EventTypeChoice, From, To, RestaurantClock);

        _events = await Explorer.ListAsync(_query.Filter, ListCap, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The line above the list. It says whether the count is the whole truth: at <see cref="ListCap"/>
    /// there may be more, and §11.4 means the page has to admit that rather than let a round number look
    /// like an answer.
    /// </summary>
    private string CountSentence(int count)
    {
        string noun = count == 1 ? "event" : "events";
        string scope = _query.IsNarrowed ? "matching the filter" : "in total";

        return count == ListCap
            ? $"{count} {noun} {scope} — capped at {ListCap}; narrow the filter to see past it."
            : $"{count} {noun} {scope}.";
    }

    /// <summary>The badge link: this same view, restricted to the row's own stream.</summary>
    private string OnlyThisStreamPath(ExplorerEvent entry) => _query.PathWithStreams(
        entry.Stream == EventStream.Security,
        entry.Stream == EventStream.Order,
        entry.Stream == EventStream.Menu);

    /// <summary>
    /// Where the row's subject lives. Security and menu events name their subject directly; an order
    /// event's subject is one guest's order, and the screen that renders an order in full is its
    /// sitting's (§11.4), so that is where it points. A stream this build does not know about gets no
    /// link rather than a guessed one.
    /// </summary>
    private static string? SubjectPath(ExplorerEvent entry) => entry.Stream switch
    {
        EventStream.Security => $"/administration/people/{entry.SubjectIdentifier}",
        EventStream.Menu => $"/administration/menu/{entry.SubjectIdentifier}",
        EventStream.Order => entry.ContextIdentifier is { } sittingIdentifier
            ? $"/administration/sittings/{sittingIdentifier}"
            : null,
        _ => null,
    };

    private static string StreamLabel(string stream) => stream switch
    {
        EventStream.Security => "Security",
        EventStream.Order => "Order",
        EventStream.Menu => "Menu",
        _ => stream,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the row, chosen by stream. Every branch falls back to the stored string, and
    /// so does the stream switch itself: §11.4 requires this screen to render what is actually in the
    /// tables, and a word this build has not caught up with must appear as itself rather than as a lie or
    /// a crash. The same rule, and mostly the same words, as ManageSitting's and HiddenRecords'.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeEvent(ExplorerEvent entry) => entry.Stream switch
    {
        EventStream.Security => DescribeSecurityEventType(entry.EventType),
        EventStream.Order => DescribeOrderEventType(entry.EventType),
        EventStream.Menu => DescribeMenuEventType(entry.EventType),
        _ => entry.EventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The nineteen <c>security_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits (§3.4–§3.7). "TOTP" is
    /// spelled "authenticator" here for the same reason the enrollment pages spell it that way: the
    /// person reading this screen manages a restaurant, and the acronym is a protocol name.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeSecurityEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "account_created" => "Account created",
        "account_deactivated" => "Account deactivated",
        "account_reactivated" => "Account reactivated",
        "password_changed" => "Password changed",
        "password_reset_by_administrator" => "Password reset by an administrator",
        "forced_password_change_completed" => "Forced password change completed",
        "totp_enrolled" => "Authenticator enrolled",
        "totp_removed" => "Authenticator removed",
        "totp_cleared_by_administrator" => "Authenticator cleared by an administrator",
        "forced_totp_enrollment_completed" => "Forced authenticator enrollment completed",
        "recovery_code_used" => "Recovery code used",
        "recovery_codes_regenerated" => "Recovery codes regenerated",
        "passkey_registered" => "Passkey registered",
        "passkey_removed" => "Passkey removed",
        "role_granted" => "Role granted",
        "role_revoked" => "Role revoked",
        "sign_in_succeeded" => "Signed in",
        "sign_in_failed" => "Sign-in failed",
        "account_locked_out" => "Account locked out",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>The five <c>order_event.event_type</c> values, in HiddenRecords' words.</summary>
    private static string DescribeOrderEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "guest_submission" => "Guest send",
        "staff_edit" => "Staff edit",
        "price_adjustment" => "Price change",
        "fulfillment" => "Delivered",
        "fulfillment_reversal" => "Delivery undone",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>The five <c>menu_item_event.event_type</c> values (§7, §8.2).</summary>
    private static string DescribeMenuEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "created" => "Item created",
        "name_changed" => "Renamed",
        "price_changed" => "Repriced",
        "activated" => "Back on the menu",
        "deactivated" => "Off the menu (86'd)",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The four <c>order_event.actor_role</c> values. <c>guest</c> is a capacity rather than a stored
    /// role (§0, §3.7) — an administrator eating lunch appears here as a guest, and that is correct.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeActorRole(string actorRole) => actorRole switch
    {
        "guest" => "a guest",
        "kitchen" => "the kitchen",
        "counter" => "the counter",
        "administrator" => "an administrator",
        _ => actorRole,
    };

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);
}

@page "/administration/hidden-records"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]

@* The hidden-records view (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §6.8, §11.4).

   §6.8's second half, verbatim: "Administrators locate hidden orders in the **hidden-records view**
   (§11.4): every currently-hidden order system-wide, filterable by username, date range, and table, each
   row expandable to the complete stored record — full event log, visibility log, sitting context,
   unprojected — with a per-record Unhide (appends `unhidden_by_administrator`)."

   This is the only unhide path in the system. §6.8 gives the hide to the owner and says plainly that
   there is no user-facing undo, so a guest who hides the wrong meal has exactly one recourse: ask a
   manager, who arrives here.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. The filter is a plain GET form — a filter is a
   bookmarkable question, not a mutation, so it belongs in the URL rather than in component state, and a
   GET form needs no antiforgery token and no handler. The Unhide is a POST that redirects back to the
   same filtered URL (post/redirect/get), so a refresh cannot re-append.

   **Expansion is one row at a time, by URL.** §11.4 requires the complete record — "never projected or
   truncated" — and a complete record is three queries per order. Rendering fifty of them to draw a list
   would be two hundred round trips for a page somebody is skimming. ?record={order} is the "expandable"
   in §6.8: the list is always complete, and the record of the row an administrator actually opened is
   fetched in full. That is narrowing on explicit request in the direction §11.4 asks for. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How many hidden orders the list will draw. §11.4's rule is that administration sees everything and
    /// narrows "only on explicit request", so this is a rendering bound rather than a filter: when it is
    /// reached the page says so and points at the filter, instead of silently answering a smaller
    /// question.
    /// </summary>
    private const int ListCap = 100;

    /// <summary>What an <c>&lt;input type="date"&gt;</c> submits, and the only format read back.</summary>
    private const string DatePattern = "yyyy-MM-dd";

    /// <summary>The one field the POST handler reads; the order travels in a hidden input.</summary>
    private const string OrderField = "order";

    private IReadOnlyList<RestaurantTableSummary> _tables = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<HiddenOrderSummary>? _hidden;
    private HiddenOrderFilter _filter = HiddenOrderFilter.Everything;

    // Only populated for the one row ?record= names.
    private SittingOrderRecord? _record;
    private CounterSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private IReadOnlyList<OrderVisibilityEntry> _visibilityLog = [];

    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private string? _dateProblem;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Username { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? From { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? To { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private Guid? Table { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private Guid? Record { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        await LoadAsync();

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;

        _tables = await Tables.ListTablesAsync(cancellationToken);
        _filter = BuildFilter();
        _hidden = await History.ListHiddenOrdersAsync(_filter, ListCap, cancellationToken);

        _record = null;
        _sitting = null;
        _visibilityLog = [];

        if (Record is not { } guestOrderIdentifier)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Only expand a row that is actually in the list. A ?record= naming an order that is not hidden —
        // or not there at all — would otherwise render a full record with an Unhide button under a list
        // that does not contain it, which reads as though the list were wrong.
        HiddenOrderSummary? summary = _hidden
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier);

        if (summary is null)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                "That record is not in the list below — it may have been unhidden already, or the filter " +
                "may exclude it. Clear the filter to look again.";
            return;
        }

        _record = await SittingRecords.GetOrderRecordAsync(guestOrderIdentifier, cancellationToken);
        _visibilityLog = await History.ListVisibilityLogAsync(guestOrderIdentifier, cancellationToken);
        _sitting = await CounterReads.GetSittingAsync(summary.SittingIdentifier, cancellationToken);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.8's three filters, from the query string. The dates are read in the restaurant's own zone
    /// through <see cref="RestaurantTime"/> (§8.1): an administrator typing 26 July means the
    /// restaurant's 26 July, and the range is half-open — the start of that day to the start of the day
    /// after the upper bound — so the last microsecond of an evening cannot fall outside it.
    /// </summary>
    private HiddenOrderFilter BuildFilter()
    {
        DateOnly? from = ParseDate(From, "the earlier date");
        DateOnly? to = ParseDate(To, "the later date");

        if (from is { } lower && to is { } upper && upper < lower)
        {
            _dateProblem =
                "The later date is before the earlier one, so the range was ignored. Swap them, or clear " +
                "one of the two.";
            from = null;
            to = null;
        }

        return new HiddenOrderFilter(
            Username,
            from is { } start ? RestaurantClock.StartOfDay(start) : null,
            to is { } end ? RestaurantClock.StartOfNextDay(end) : null,
            Table);
    }

    private DateOnly? ParseDate(string? value, string which)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value))
        {
            return null;
        }

        if (DateOnly.TryParseExact(
                value.Trim(), DatePattern, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None,
                out DateOnly parsed))
        {
            return parsed;
        }

        // Only reachable from a hand-edited URL: the date input submits yyyy-MM-dd or nothing at all.
        _dateProblem = $"Could not read {which}, so it was ignored. Dates are year-month-day.";
        return null;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.8's per-record Unhide, through the workflow so the change is announced (§9) and the owner's
    /// history page stops omitting it. The service re-checks under its own lock that the order is still
    /// hidden, so two administrators pressing this at once produce one <c>unhidden</c> row and one honest
    /// "somebody got there first".
    /// </summary>
    private async Task UnhideAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that brace,
            // because order_visibility_event.actor_person_identifier is NOT NULL and has no anonymous
            // option.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        IFormCollection form = await HttpContext.Request.ReadFormAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Not a second read of the body: the Blazor endpoint has already parsed the form to find this
        // handler, and HttpRequest caches the parsed collection. Same shape as AdministrationSittings.
        string? postedOrder = form[OrderField];

        if (!Guid.TryParse(postedOrder, out Guid guestOrderIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That request did not name a record, so nothing was unhidden.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        UnhideOrderResult result = await Visibility.UnhideAsync(
            guestOrderIdentifier, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome is UnhideOrderOutcome.Unhidden or UnhideOrderOutcome.NotHidden)
        {
            // Post/redirect/get, back to the same filtered list minus the expanded row — the record is no
            // longer hidden, so it is no longer on this page, and leaving ?record= on the URL would only
            // produce the "not in the list" message. NotHidden redirects too: another administrator got
            // there first, which is the system working.
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ListPath(
                result.Outcome is UnhideOrderOutcome.Unhidden ? "unhidden" : "already-visible"));
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage =
            "That order no longer exists, so there was nothing to unhide. Reload the page to see the " +
            "current list.";
        await LoadAsync();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The list URL with the current filter preserved and, optionally, an outcome word. Rebuilt rather
    /// than reusing the incoming query string so <c>?record=</c> is dropped and nothing else is.
    /// </summary>
    /// <summary>Whether this row is the one <c>?record=</c> named and the record was actually loaded for.</summary>
    private bool IsExpanded(HiddenOrderSummary summary)
        => Record == summary.GuestOrderIdentifier;

    /// <summary>
    /// The line above the list. It says whether the count is the whole truth: at <see cref="ListCap"/>
    /// there may be more, and §11.4 means the page has to admit that rather than let a round number look
    /// like an answer.
    /// </summary>
    private string CountSentence(int count)
    {
        string noun = count == 1 ? "hidden order" : "hidden orders";
        string scope = _filter.IsNarrowed ? "matching the filter" : "in total";

        return count == ListCap
            ? $"{count} {noun} {scope} — capped at {ListCap}; narrow the filter to see past it."
            : $"{count} {noun} {scope}.";
    }

    private string ListPath(string? done = null)
    {
        List<string> parts = [];

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Username))
        {
            parts.Add($"username={Uri.EscapeDataString(Username.Trim())}");
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(From))
        {
            parts.Add($"from={Uri.EscapeDataString(From.Trim())}");
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(To))
        {
            parts.Add($"to={Uri.EscapeDataString(To.Trim())}");
        }

        if (Table is { } tableIdentifier)
        {
            parts.Add($"table={tableIdentifier}");
        }

        if (done is not null)
        {
            parts.Add($"done={done}");
        }

        return parts.Count == 0
            ? "/administration/hidden-records"
            : $"/administration/hidden-records?{string.Join("&", parts)}";
    }

    private string RecordPath(HiddenOrderSummary summary)
    {
        string list = ListPath();
        string separator = list.Contains('?', StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "&" : "?";

        return $"{list}{separator}record={summary.GuestOrderIdentifier}";
    }

    private static string SittingPath(HiddenOrderSummary summary)
        => $"/administration/sittings/{summary.SittingIdentifier}";

    private static string? FlashFor(string? done) => done switch
    {
        "unhidden" =>
            "Unhidden. It is back on its owner's history page, and the visibility log records that you " +
            "put it there.",
        "already-visible" =>
            "It was not hidden any more — another administrator had already unhidden it, so nothing was " +
            "appended.",
        _ => null,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The two <c>order_visibility_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits, falling back to the
    /// stored string. §6.8's prose calls the administrator's row "unhidden_by_administrator"; the stored
    /// word is <c>unhidden</c>, and there is no guest unhide to distinguish it from, so who did it is the
    /// actor beside it rather than a second word.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeVisibilityEvent(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "hidden" => "Hidden by the owner",
        "unhidden" => "Restored by an administrator",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the five <c>order_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits, falling
    /// back to the stored string for anything else. The words are spelled out here rather than taken from
    /// <c>OrderEventVocabulary</c>, which is internal to the data-access assembly on purpose — a display
    /// label is not the writer's business, and a reader that threw on an unrecognised word would blank the
    /// one page whose job is to show what is actually stored. Same shape as ManageSitting's.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "guest_submission" => "Guest send",
        "staff_edit" => "Staff edit",
        "price_adjustment" => "Price change",
        "fulfillment" => "Delivered",
        "fulfillment_reversal" => "Delivery undone",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The four <c>order_event.actor_role</c> values, on the same terms. <c>guest</c> is a capacity rather
    /// than a stored role (§0, §3.7) — an administrator eating lunch appears here as a guest, and that is
    /// correct.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeActorRole(string actorRole) => actorRole switch
    {
        "guest" => "a guest",
        "kitchen" => "the kitchen",
        "counter" => "the counter",
        "administrator" => "an administrator",
        _ => actorRole,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// One stored operation in a sentence. The five kinds are the discriminators the reader's UNION
    /// projects; an unknown one renders as itself beside the line it names, so nothing is ever swallowed.
    /// </summary>
    private string DescribeOperation(StoredOrderOperation operation) => operation.OperationKind switch
    {
        "line_added" =>
            $"Added {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} at " +
            $"{Money(operation.UnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{NoteSuffix(operation.CustomizationNote)}",
        "line_removed" =>
            $"Removed {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_price_adjusted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} repriced to " +
            $"{Money(operation.NewUnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_fulfilled" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} delivered",
        "line_fulfillment_reverted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} put back with the kitchen",
        _ => $"{operation.OperationKind} on {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}",
    };

    private static string NoteSuffix(string? note)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(note) ? string.Empty : $" — “{note.Trim()}”";

    private static string ReasonSuffix(string? reason)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(reason) ? string.Empty : $" — {reason.Trim()}";

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);
}
