@* This page declares nothing. Its facts grid, its chips, its headings, its rules, its inline forms, its
   currency unit and — as of M6 Slice 34 — its history list are all app.css's §11.12 vocabulary. This was
   one of four pages carrying an inline copy of that vocabulary, and the copies had drifted (F-66); the
   history table was also the page's own eighty-line table rules under a different name.

   The section picker needed no new rule either: `.manage-inline-form` has styled `select` since Slice 34,
   which is why the comment beside the description form says that class has never styled a `textarea` —
   the two statements are the same sentence read from opposite ends. No count of the forms on this page is
   written here, on F-77's ruling; the previous version of this note said TWO and there were four. *@

@code {
    private MenuItemSummary? _item;
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuSectionSummary> _sections = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemEventEntry>? _history;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid MenuItemId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-rename")]
    private RenameInputModel RenameInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-reprice")]
    private RepriceInputModel RepriceInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-describe")]
    private DescribeInputModel DescribeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-move-section")]
    private MoveInputModel MoveInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-reorder")]
    private ReorderInputModel ReorderInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/menu/{MenuItemId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so the defaults live here.
        RenameInput ??= new();
        RepriceInput ??= new();
        DescribeInput ??= new();
        MoveInput ??= new();
        ReorderInput ??= new();

        _item = await MenuItems.GetAsync(MenuItemId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_item is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Every heading, active and inactive, in display order — §11.4's administrator sees the ones no
        // guest can reach, which is precisely where next week's menu gets stocked.
        _sections = await MenuSections.ListAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        _history = await MenuEvents.ListForItemAsync(MenuItemId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // On GET, pre-fill both editors with what is stored and render any post/redirect flash. On POST
        // the submitted values are already bound, so they must not be overwritten.
        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RenameInput.Name))
            {
                RenameInput.Name = _item.Name;
            }

            RepriceInput.PriceAmount = _item.PriceAmount;

            // Unlike the name, an empty description is a legitimate stored value, so `IsNullOrEmpty`
            // cannot tell "nothing bound yet" from "the item has none" — and it does not need to: on a
            // GET nothing has bound, so assigning unconditionally is both correct and simpler.
            DescribeInput.Description = _item.Description;
            ReorderInput.DisplayOrder = _item.DisplayOrder;

            // Pre-selected on the heading the item is already under, so the form opens showing the truth
            // and submitting it unchanged is the no-op the write service reports rather than a move to
            // whichever heading happened to sort first. CreateMenuItem pre-selects for the mirror-image
            // reason: a <select> with nothing selected shows and posts its first option either way.
            MoveInput.MenuSectionIdentifier = _item.MenuSectionIdentifier;

            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task RenameAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        RenameMenuItemResult result = await MenuChanges.RenameMenuItemAsync(
            MenuItemId, RenameInput.Name.Trim(), administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (result.Outcome)
        {
            case RenameMenuItemOutcome.Renamed:
                RedirectWithOutcome("renamed");
                break;
            case RenameMenuItemOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("rename-no-change");
                break;
            case RenameMenuItemOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RepriceAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        RepriceMenuItemResult result = await MenuChanges.RepriceMenuItemAsync(
            MenuItemId, RepriceInput.PriceAmount, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (result.Outcome)
        {
            case RepriceMenuItemOutcome.Repriced:
                RedirectWithOutcome("repriced");
                break;
            case RepriceMenuItemOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("reprice-no-change");
                break;
            case RepriceMenuItemOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task DescribeAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        DescribeMenuItemOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.DescribeMenuItemAsync(
            MenuItemId, DescribeInput.Description, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case DescribeMenuItemOutcome.Described:
                RedirectWithOutcome(
                    DescribeInput.Description.Trim().Length == 0 ? "description-cleared" : "described");
                break;
            case DescribeMenuItemOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("describe-no-change");
                break;
            case DescribeMenuItemOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task MoveAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync(
            MenuItemId, MoveInput.MenuSectionIdentifier, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome.Moved:
                RedirectWithOutcome("refiled");
                break;
            case MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("refile-no-change");
                break;
            case MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome.MenuSectionNotFound:
                // A heading deleted or a page left open. Reported in place rather than redirected, for
                // the reason CreateMenuItem reports the same outcome in place: the person needs to see
                // the picker beside the message, not a fresh page with no account of what happened.
                _errorMessage =
                    "That section no longer exists. It may have been changed while this page was open —"
                    + " reload the page and choose again.";
                break;
            case MoveMenuItemToSectionOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ReorderAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        ReorderMenuItemOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.ReorderMenuItemAsync(
            MenuItemId, ReorderInput.DisplayOrder, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case ReorderMenuItemOutcome.Reordered:
                RedirectWithOutcome("moved");
                break;
            case ReorderMenuItemOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("move-no-change");
                break;
            case ReorderMenuItemOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ToggleAvailabilityAsync()
    {
        if (_item is null || !TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_item.IsActive;
        SetMenuItemAvailabilityResult result = await MenuChanges.SetMenuItemActiveAsync(
            MenuItemId, target, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (result.Outcome)
        {
            case SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "made-available" : "made-unavailable");
                break;
            case SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.AlreadyInThatState:
                // Somebody in the kitchen got there first between this page rendering and the button
                // being pressed. Nothing changed and nothing is wrong; re-render on the truth.
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The two things every write on this page needs first: the item must still exist, and the acting
    /// administrator must be identifiable — <c>menu_item_event.actor_person_identifier</c> is NOT NULL and
    /// §7 requires every change to name somebody. Endpoint authorization already guarantees the second;
    /// this is the belt to that brace.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryBegin(out Guid administrator)
    {
        administrator = Guid.Empty;

        if (_item is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
            return false;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } identifier)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return false;
        }

        administrator = identifier;
        return true;
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "renamed" => "Renamed. The new name shows everywhere immediately, including on past orders.",
        "rename-no-change" => "That was already the name — nothing changed.",
        "repriced" => "Repriced. Lines already on an order keep the price they were added at.",
        "reprice-no-change" => "That was already the price — nothing changed.",
        "described" => "Description saved. Guests reading the menu see it from now on.",
        "description-cleared" => "Description cleared. Guests see the name and the price only.",
        "describe-no-change" => "That was already the description — nothing changed.",
        "refiled" => "Filed under its new heading, at the end of it. Every open menu has already"
            + " regrouped; set the position below if the end is not where it belongs.",
        "refile-no-change" => "It was already under that heading — nothing changed.",
        "moved" => "Moved. The menu is ordered by position, then by name.",
        "move-no-change" => "It was already in that position — nothing changed.",
        "made-unavailable" => "Marked unavailable. It stays on the guest's menu, labelled unavailable, and cannot be ordered.",
        "made-available" => "Marked available. It can be ordered again.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for each event type §8.2's vocabulary CHECK admits, falling back to the stored
    /// string for anything else — §11.4 renders the record, so an unrecognised type must show as itself
    /// rather than be swallowed.
    ///
    /// <para><b>No count of the vocabulary is stated.</b> It was stated as <em>five</em> in three files
    /// and <c>0004</c> made it seven; a number here is one fact recorded where nothing can check it, and
    /// the arms below are the only honest census (F-77).</para>
    ///
    /// <para><c>description_changed</c> reads differently when the description was cleared, because
    /// <c>""</c> is a stored value rather than an absence and "Description set to nothing" is not what
    /// somebody reading a history wants. The arm tests the payload's length rather than for null: the
    /// paired CHECK guarantees this type carries one, and the <c>?? string.Empty</c> is there so a row
    /// written by something that got past the constraint still renders.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string Describe(MenuItemEventEntry entry) => entry.EventType switch
    {
        "created" => $"Created as “{entry.NewName}” at {Money(entry.NewPriceAmount ?? 0m)}",
        "name_changed" => $"Renamed to “{entry.NewName}”",
        "price_changed" => $"Repriced to {Money(entry.NewPriceAmount ?? 0m)}",
        "description_changed" => (entry.NewDescription ?? string.Empty).Length == 0
            ? "Description cleared"
            : $"Description set to “{entry.NewDescription}”",
        "section_changed" => $"Filed under “{entry.NewMenuSectionName}”",
        "reordered" => $"Moved to position {entry.NewDisplayOrder}",
        "activated" => "Marked available",
        "deactivated" => "Marked unavailable",
        _ => entry.EventType,
    };

    private sealed class RenameInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a name.")]
        [StringLength(120, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The name must be 1–120 characters.")]
        public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class RepriceInputModel
    {
        [Range(0, 99999999.99, ErrorMessage = "The price must be between 0 and 99,999,999.99.")]
        public decimal PriceAmount { get; set; }
    }

    private sealed class DescribeInputModel
    {
        // No [Required]: clearing the description is a supported change. The 2,000 matches
        // CreateMenuItem's, and is this form's opinion rather than the column's — `text` has no ceiling.
        [StringLength(2000, ErrorMessage = "The description must be 2,000 characters or fewer.")]
        public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class MoveInputModel
    {
        // No [Required], for CreateMenuItem's reason rather than as an omission: Guid is a value type, so
        // [Required] passes on Guid.Empty and would assert nothing. The select is pre-selected on the
        // item's own heading, has no empty option, and the write service reports an identifier that names
        // nothing — three defences, none of which is a validation attribute that does not work.
        public Guid MenuSectionIdentifier { get; set; }
    }

    private sealed class ReorderInputModel
    {
        // The upper bound is `integer`'s, and it is stated so the form refuses what the column would.
        [Range(0, 2147483647, ErrorMessage = "The position must be 0 or greater.")]
        public int DisplayOrder { get; set; }
    }
}

@* Manage one menu section (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §7, §11.4). Administrator only (endpoint
   authorization). Static SSR: rename, describe, reposition and the on/off switch are full-page form
   posts. Successful changes redirect back here (post/redirect/get) carrying a one-word outcome so a
   refresh does not re-post; the shape ManageTable established and ManageMenuItem repeated.

   THIS PAGE IS WHAT FOUR WORKFLOW VERBS WERE WAITING FOR. Slice 37 put the section writes outside
   IMenuWorkflow deliberately, on the rule that a workflow verb with no caller is a code path no test can
   reach through the interface meant to protect it; Slice 40 brought CreateMenuSectionAsync in because the
   create page called it. Rename, describe, reorder and set-active arrive together here, because they are
   four forms on one page and shipping a subset would leave the same hole under a smaller name. Every one
   of them publishes MenuChanged on a committed row (§9) — which matters most for the last two: §11.1
   groups the guest menu by heading, and §7 hides an inactive heading from the guest entirely.

   Four forms rather than one Save, for §8.2's reason: `renamed`, `described` and `reordered` are distinct
   event types with mutually exclusive payload columns, so a combined save would write three events anyway
   and would then have to decide what to do when two of the three changed nothing.

   The history below is complete and uncapped, oldest first. §11.4: administration renders "the complete
   stored record everywhere — full event streams … never projected or truncated for the administrator". *@

@* This page declares nothing. Its facts grid, its chips, its headings, its rules, its three small forms
   and its two record lists are all app.css's §11.12 vocabulary. A new page is exactly where a fifth
   inline copy of that vocabulary would appear (F-66), which is why this note is here rather than in a
   commit message. *@

@code {
    private MenuSectionSummary? _section;
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _items = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuSectionEventEntry>? _history;
    private int _itemCount;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid MenuSectionId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-section-rename")]
    private RenameInputModel RenameInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-section-describe")]
    private DescribeInputModel DescribeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-section-reorder")]
    private ReorderInputModel ReorderInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/menu/sections/{MenuSectionId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so the defaults live here.
        RenameInput ??= new();
        DescribeInput ??= new();
        ReorderInput ??= new();

        _section = await MenuSections.GetAsync(MenuSectionId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_section is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Filtered here rather than asked for by section, because IMenuDirectory has no per-section read
        // and inventing one would be a query with a single caller. The menu is single-digit-to-sixty rows
        // on the machine this runs on, and its ordering already puts one heading's items contiguously —
        // so the filter preserves the order guests see without re-deciding it (§7).
        IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> everything = await MenuItems.ListAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        _items = everything.Where(item => item.MenuSectionIdentifier == MenuSectionId).ToArray();
        _itemCount = _items.Count;

        _history = await MenuSectionEvents.ListForSectionAsync(MenuSectionId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // On GET, pre-fill each editor with what is stored and render any post/redirect flash. On POST the
        // submitted values are already bound, so they must not be overwritten.
        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RenameInput.Name))
            {
                RenameInput.Name = _section.Name;
            }

            // Unlike the name, an empty description is a legitimate stored value, so `IsNullOrEmpty`
            // cannot tell "nothing bound yet" from "this heading has none" — and it does not need to: on
            // a GET nothing has bound, so assigning unconditionally is both correct and simpler.
            DescribeInput.Description = _section.Description;
            ReorderInput.DisplayOrder = _section.DisplayOrder;

            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task RenameAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        RenameMenuSectionOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.RenameMenuSectionAsync(
            MenuSectionId, RenameInput.Name.Trim(), administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RenameMenuSectionOutcome.Renamed:
                RedirectWithOutcome("renamed");
                break;
            case RenameMenuSectionOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("rename-no-change");
                break;
            case RenameMenuSectionOutcome.NameTaken:
                // Reported in place rather than redirected, because the person needs to see what they
                // typed beside the message. The check is citext, so the collision may be with a heading
                // spelled differently — which is exactly the case a bare "taken" would leave baffling.
                _errorMessage =
                    "Another section already uses that name. Section names ignore capitalisation, so"
                    + " check the menu for one spelled differently.";
                break;
            case RenameMenuSectionOutcome.MenuSectionNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task DescribeAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        DescribeMenuSectionOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.DescribeMenuSectionAsync(
            MenuSectionId, DescribeInput.Description, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case DescribeMenuSectionOutcome.Described:
                RedirectWithOutcome(
                    DescribeInput.Description.Trim().Length == 0 ? "description-cleared" : "described");
                break;
            case DescribeMenuSectionOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("describe-no-change");
                break;
            case DescribeMenuSectionOutcome.MenuSectionNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ReorderAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        ReorderMenuSectionOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.ReorderMenuSectionAsync(
            MenuSectionId, ReorderInput.DisplayOrder, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case ReorderMenuSectionOutcome.Reordered:
                RedirectWithOutcome("moved");
                break;
            case ReorderMenuSectionOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("move-no-change");
                break;
            case ReorderMenuSectionOutcome.MenuSectionNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ToggleVisibilityAsync()
    {
        if (_section is null || !TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_section.IsActive;
        MenuSectionActivationOutcome outcome = await MenuChanges.SetMenuSectionActiveAsync(
            MenuSectionId, target, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case MenuSectionActivationOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "shown" : "hidden");
                break;
            case MenuSectionActivationOutcome.NoChange:
                // Somebody else got there first between this page rendering and the button being pressed.
                // Nothing changed and nothing is wrong; re-render on the truth.
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case MenuSectionActivationOutcome.MenuSectionNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The two things every write on this page needs first: the section must still exist, and the acting
    /// administrator must be identifiable — <c>menu_section_event.actor_person_identifier</c> is NOT NULL
    /// and §7 requires every change to name somebody. Endpoint authorization already guarantees the
    /// second; this is the belt to that brace. The same helper <c>ManageMenuItem</c> carries, one table
    /// over.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryBegin(out Guid administrator)
    {
        administrator = Guid.Empty;

        if (_section is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
            return false;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } identifier)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return false;
        }

        administrator = identifier;
        return true;
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "renamed" => "Renamed. Every open menu has already picked up the new heading.",
        "rename-no-change" => "That was already the name — nothing changed.",
        "described" => "Description saved.",
        "description-cleared" => "Description cleared. The heading stands on its own.",
        "describe-no-change" => "That was already the description — nothing changed.",
        "moved" => "Moved. The menu is ordered by position, then by name.",
        "move-no-change" => "It was already in that position — nothing changed.",
        "hidden" => "Hidden from guests. This heading and everything under it have left every open menu;"
            + " the items themselves are untouched.",
        "shown" => "Showing to guests again, with every item exactly as it was.",
        _ => null,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for each event type §8.2's <c>menu_section_event</c> CHECK admits, falling back to
    /// the stored string for anything else — §11.4 renders the record, so an unrecognised type must show
    /// as itself rather than be swallowed.
    ///
    /// <para><b>No count of the vocabulary is stated</b>, on F-77's ruling: the arms below are the only
    /// census that cannot go stale, and a number in this sentence is one fact recorded where nothing in
    /// the tree can check it.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><c>activated</c> and <c>deactivated</c> are worded as what a guest sees rather than as what
    /// the column says, matching the chip at the top of the page. §7's two <c>is_active</c> flags do
    /// opposite things one table apart, and a history that said "Deactivated" would read identically to an
    /// item's — which is precisely the confusion this page exists to prevent.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><c>described</c> reads differently when the description was cleared, because <c>""</c> is a
    /// stored value rather than an absence. The arm tests the payload's length rather than for null: the
    /// paired CHECK guarantees this type carries one, and the <c>?? string.Empty</c> is there so a row
    /// written by something that got past the constraint still renders.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private static string Describe(MenuSectionEventEntry entry) => entry.EventType switch
    {
        "created" => $"Created as “{entry.NewName}” at position {entry.NewDisplayOrder}",
        "renamed" => $"Renamed to “{entry.NewName}”",
        "described" => (entry.NewDescription ?? string.Empty).Length == 0
            ? "Description cleared"
            : $"Description set to “{entry.NewDescription}”",
        "reordered" => $"Moved to position {entry.NewDisplayOrder}",
        "activated" => "Shown to guests",
        "deactivated" => "Hidden from guests",
        _ => entry.EventType,
    };

    private sealed class RenameInputModel
    {
        // The 80 is the column's own ceiling: menu_section.name is CHECK (char_length BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
        // so a longer name would be PostgreSQL error 23514 well after the form that caused it. The same
        // limit CreateMenuSection states, for the same reason.
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Give the section a name.")]
        [StringLength(80, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The name must be 1–80 characters.")]
        public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class DescribeInputModel
    {
        // No [Required]: clearing the description is a supported change. The 2,000 is this form's own
        // limit rather than the column's — menu_section.description is `text` and has none — and it
        // matches CreateMenuSection's.
        [StringLength(2000, ErrorMessage = "The description must be 2,000 characters or fewer.")]
        public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class ReorderInputModel
    {
        // The upper bound is `integer`'s, stated so the form refuses what the column would.
        [Range(0, 2147483647, ErrorMessage = "The position must be 0 or greater.")]
        public int DisplayOrder { get; set; }
    }
}

   small forms are all app.css's §11.12 vocabulary — this was one of four pages carrying an inline copy
   of it, and the copies had drifted (F-66). `.staff-temporary-password` still has no rule behind it and

@code {
    private static readonly string[] AllStaffRoles =
        [RestaurantRoles.Administrator, RestaurantRoles.Counter, RestaurantRoles.Kitchen];

    private PersonSummary? _person;
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _grantableRoles = [];
    private bool _isSelf;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    private CredentialResetResult? _resetResult;
    private string? _temporaryPassword;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid PersonId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-grant-role")]
    private RoleSelectionModel GrantInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-revoke-role")]
    private RoleSelectionModel RevokeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/people/{PersonId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: form POSTs bind these themselves and may assign null, so defaults live here.
        GrantInput ??= new();
        RevokeInput ??= new();

        _person = await People.GetPersonAsync(PersonId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_person is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _grantableRoles = AllStaffRoles.Where(role => !_person.Roles.Contains(role)).ToArray();

        Person? actingAdministrator = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        _isSelf = actingAdministrator is not null && actingAdministrator.PersonIdentifier == _person.PersonIdentifier;

        // Render the flash for a completed action after the post/redirect/get, on GET only.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task GrantRoleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(GrantInput.RoleName))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose a role to grant.";
            return;
        }

        RoleGrantOutcome outcome = await Accounts.GrantRoleAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, GrantInput.RoleName, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RoleGrantOutcome.Granted:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-granted");
                break;
            case RoleGrantOutcome.AlreadyHeld:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-already-held");
                break;
            case RoleGrantOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RevokeRoleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RevokeInput.RoleName))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose a role to revoke.";
            return;
        }

        RoleRevokeOutcome outcome = await Accounts.RevokeRoleAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, RevokeInput.RoleName, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.Revoked:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-revoked");
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.NotHeld:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-not-held");
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.WouldRemoveLastAdministrator:
                _errorMessage = "This is the only administrator, so the administrator role cannot be removed. "
                    + "Grant administrator to someone else first.";
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ResetCredentialsAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Generate + hash the temporary password here so the plaintext is only ever held for the one
        // response that shows it (§3.2). 12 random bytes → a 16-character URL-safe string.
        string temporaryPassword = SecretGenerator.GenerateBase64UrlSecret(12);
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = _person.PersonIdentifier, Username = _person.Username },
            temporaryPassword);

        CredentialResetResult result = await Accounts.ResetCredentialsAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, passwordHash, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == CredentialResetOutcome.PersonNotFound)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
            return;
        }

        // Show the temporary password once, in this response (no redirect).
        _temporaryPassword = temporaryPassword;
        _resetResult = result;
    }

    private async Task ToggleActivationAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_person.IsActive;
        AccountActivationOutcome outcome = await Accounts.SetAccountActiveAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, target, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case AccountActivationOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "account-reactivated" : "account-deactivated");
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.NoChange:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.WouldDeactivateLastAdministrator:
                _errorMessage = "This is the only administrator that can sign in, so it cannot be deactivated. "
                    + "Make sure another administrator is active first.";
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "role-granted" => "Role granted. It takes effect on their sessions within a few minutes.",
        "role-already-held" => "That role was already held — nothing changed.",
        "role-revoked" => "Role revoked. It takes effect on their sessions within a few minutes.",
        "role-not-held" => "That role was not held — nothing changed.",
        "account-deactivated" => "Account deactivated. Its sessions end within a few minutes.",
        "account-reactivated" => "Account reactivated.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private bool IsLockedOut(PersonSummary person)
        => person.LockoutEndAt is { } end && end > Clock.UtcNow;

    private static string Capitalize(string role)
        => string.IsNullOrEmpty(role) ? role : char.ToUpperInvariant(role[0]) + role[1..];

    private sealed class RoleSelectionModel
    {
        public string RoleName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@* One sitting's complete stored record, and the corrections an administrator may append to it
   (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §5.3, §6.7, §11.4).

   §11.4 is emphatic about what this page owes its reader: "Administration renders the complete stored
   record everywhere — full event streams, visibility logs, security events — never projected or truncated
   for the administrator; filters narrow only on explicit request." So the history below is every event on
   every order in the sitting, oldest first, uncapped, including the removals, the reverted fulfillments,
   and the prices that were superseded. A settled bill is the thing people argue about, and an argument is
   settled by reading forward from the first send.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. Corrections are full-page form posts that redirect back
   here (post/redirect/get) carrying a one-word outcome, so a refresh cannot re-append.

   **The corrective controls appear only once the sitting is settled.** §6.7 is titled "post-close
   corrections" and §3.7's matrix gives "post-close corrective events" to the administrator alone; while a
   table is still eating, the screen built for it is the counter's, and an administrator already holds the
   counter role's capabilities (§3.7), so this page links there instead of growing a second copy of it.
   The record itself renders either way — an administrator reading an open table's history is not a write. *@

                <em>after</em> a close (§6.7). To adjust a price, take a line off, or settle the bill while
                the table is still here, use the counter screen; you already hold that capability.
            </p>
            <div class="form-actions">
                <a class="button-primary" href="@CounterPath">Open at the counter</a>
            </div>
        }

        @* ---- who was at the table (§5.1, §5.2) -------------------------------------------------- *@
        <hr class="record-rule" />

        <h2 class="record-heading">At the table</h2>
        @if (_members.Count == 0)
        {
            <p class="lede">Nobody is recorded as having joined this sitting.</p>
        }
        else
        {
            <ul class="sitting-roster">
                @foreach (SittingMemberSummary member in _members)
                {
                    <li>
                        <span class="sitting-roster-name">@member.RosterName</span>
                        <span class="record-secondary">
                            joined @RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(member.JoinedAt)
                            @if (!HasAnOrder(member.PersonIdentifier))
                            {
                                <text> · never ordered</text>
                            }
                        </span>
                    </li>
                }
            </ul>
        }

        @* ---- the bill, person by person (§8.3) --------------------------------------------------- *@
        <h2 class="record-heading">The bill</h2>
        @if (_bill.Count == 0)
        {
            <p class="lede">Nothing was ordered on this table.</p>
        }
        else
        {
            <div class="record-list">
                <table>
                    <thead>
                        <tr>
                            <th scope="col">Guest</th>
                            <th scope="col">Current lines</th>
                            <th scope="col">Total now</th>
                        </tr>
                    </thead>
                    <tbody>
                        @foreach (SittingBillEntry entry in _bill)
                        {
                            <tr @key="entry.GuestOrderIdentifier">
                                <td class="record-primary" data-label="">@entry.BillName</td>
                                <td data-label="Current lines">
                                    @if (LinesFor(entry.GuestOrderIdentifier).Count == 0)
                                    {
                                        <span class="record-secondary">Every line was removed</span>
                                    }
                                    else
                                    {
                                        <ul class="sitting-lines">
                                            @foreach (OrderLineView line in LinesFor(entry.GuestOrderIdentifier))
                                            {
                                                <li>
                                                    @line.Quantity × @line.MenuItemName
                                                    <span class="record-secondary">
                                                        @Money(line.CurrentUnitPriceAmount) each ·
                                                        @(line.IsFulfilled ? "delivered" : "still with the kitchen")
                                                        @if (line.CustomizationNote is { } note)
                                                        {
                                                            <text> · “@note”</text>
                                                        }
                                                    </span>
                                                </li>
                                            }
                                        </ul>
                                    }
                                </td>
                                <td class="record-numeric" data-label="Total now">@Money(entry.PersonTotalAmount)</td>
                            </tr>
                        }
                    </tbody>
                </table>
            </div>

            <p class="sitting-tally">
                <span>Current total across the table</span>
                <strong class="record-numeric">@Money(TableTotal)</strong>
            </p>
        }

        @* ---- post-close corrections (§6.7) ------------------------------------------------------- *@
        @if (!_sitting.IsOpen)
        {
            <hr class="record-rule" />

            <h2 class="record-heading">Corrections</h2>
            <p class="lede">
                Appended events, never edits. The settled total above stays exactly as it was stamped;
                everything written here lives beside it and shows as the corrected total (§5.3, §6.7).
                Every correction records you as the actor and is permanent — a mistaken correction is
                undone by appending another, not by removing this one.
            </p>

            @if (_lines.Count == 0)
            {
                <p class="lede">There is no line on this bill to correct.</p>
            }
            else
            {
                <h3 class="manage-subheading">Correct a line</h3>
                <EditForm Model="CorrectInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="CorrectLineAsync"
                          FormName="sitting-correct-line">
                    <DataAnnotationsValidator />

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="correct-line">Line</label>
                        <InputSelect id="correct-line" @bind-Value="CorrectInput.OrderLineIdentifier">
                            <option value="">Choose a line…</option>
                            @foreach (OrderLineView line in _lines)
                            {
                                <option value="@line.OrderLineIdentifier">@LineOptionLabel(line)</option>
                            }
                        </InputSelect>
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => CorrectInput.OrderLineIdentifier)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="correct-action">What to do</label>
                        <InputSelect id="correct-action" @bind-Value="CorrectInput.Action">
                            <option value="@AdjustAction">Change the price</option>
                            <option value="@RemoveAction">Take it off the bill</option>
                        </InputSelect>
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => CorrectInput.Action)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="correct-price">
                            New unit price <span class="optional">(@Options.CurrencyCode — price changes only)</span>
                        </label>
                        <InputNumber id="correct-price" @bind-Value="CorrectInput.NewUnitPriceAmount"
                                     step="0.01" min="0" inputmode="decimal" />
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => CorrectInput.NewUnitPriceAmount)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="correct-reason">
                            Reason
                            <span class="optional">(required for a price change, optional for a removal)</span>
                        </label>
                        <InputText id="correct-reason" @bind-Value="CorrectInput.Reason" autocomplete="off" />
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => CorrectInput.Reason)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-actions">
                        <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Append the correction</button>
                    </div>
                </EditForm>

                <p class="form-footnote">
                    A price change needs a reason because <c>order_operation_line_price_adjusted.reason</c>
                    is NOT NULL and CHECK-constrained against blanks (§8.2) — it is the sentence somebody
                    reads back in six months. A removal's reason is optional, and is still worth writing.
                </p>
            }

            <h3 class="manage-subheading">Add a line that was missed</h3>
            <p class="lede">
                For the plate that went out and never reached a bill. It joins the order of whoever you
                name — creating that order if they never sent anything themselves (§6.1) — and is priced
                from the menu at the moment it is written, not from this screen (§6.5.4). To charge
                something else, add it and then change its price with a reason.
            </p>

            @if (_peopleAtTheTable.Count == 0)
            {
                <p class="lede">Nobody is recorded at this table, so there is nobody to bill.</p>
            }
            else
            {
                <EditForm Model="AddInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="AddLineAsync" FormName="sitting-add-line">
                    <DataAnnotationsValidator />

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="add-person">For</label>
                        <InputSelect id="add-person" @bind-Value="AddInput.PersonIdentifier">
                            <option value="">Choose a guest…</option>
                            @foreach (BillablePerson person in _peopleAtTheTable)
                            {
                                <option value="@person.PersonIdentifier">@person.Name</option>
                            }
                        </InputSelect>
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AddInput.PersonIdentifier)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="add-item">Item</label>
                        <InputSelect id="add-item" @bind-Value="AddInput.MenuItemIdentifier">
                            <option value="">Choose an item…</option>
                            @foreach (MenuItemSummary item in _menu)
                            {
                                <option value="@item.MenuItemIdentifier" disabled="@(!item.IsActive)">
                                    @ItemOptionLabel(item)
                                </option>
                            }
                        </InputSelect>
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AddInput.MenuItemIdentifier)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="add-quantity">Quantity</label>
                        <InputNumber id="add-quantity" @bind-Value="AddInput.Quantity" min="1" max="100" />
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AddInput.Quantity)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-field">
                        <label for="add-note">Note <span class="optional">(optional)</span></label>
                        <InputText id="add-note" @bind-Value="AddInput.Note" autocomplete="off" />
                        <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AddInput.Note)" />
                    </div>

                    <div class="form-actions">
                        <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Add the line</button>
                    </div>
                </EditForm>

                <p class="form-footnote">
                    An item currently marked unavailable cannot be added — the order transaction re-checks
                    the flag under its own lock (§6.5.4), so making it available again is the only way
                    through. That is deliberate: the alternative is a bill naming a dish the kitchen has
                    said it cannot make.
                </p>
            }
        }

        @* ---- the complete stored record (§11.4) -------------------------------------------------- *@
        <hr class="record-rule" />

        <h2 class="record-heading">The record</h2>

        @if (_records.Count == 0)
        {
            <p class="lede">
                No order was ever created on this sitting, so there is no event history. People can join a
                table without ordering; the order row is created by the first send (§6.1).
            </p>
        }
        else
        {
            <p class="lede">
                Every event on every order, oldest first and complete — @_eventCount in total. Removed
                lines, undone fulfillments, and superseded prices are all still here, because the history
                outliving the state is the point of the log (ADR-0002).
            </p>

            @foreach (SittingOrderRecord orderRecord in _records)
            {
                <article class="sitting-order">
                    <header class="sitting-order-header">
                        <h3>@orderRecord.OwnerName</h3>
                        <span class="record-secondary">
                            order opened @RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(orderRecord.CreatedAt) ·
                            @orderRecord.Events.Count @(orderRecord.Events.Count == 1 ? "event" : "events")
                        </span>
                    </header>

                    @if (orderRecord.Events.Count == 0)
                    {
                        <p class="record-secondary">
                            The order row exists with no events on it. Only reachable if a write created it
                            and then rolled back its event, which the transaction does not do — worth
                            reporting if you are seeing it.
                        </p>
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        <ol class="sitting-events">
                            @foreach (StoredOrderEvent stored in orderRecord.Events)
                            {
                                <li class="sitting-event">
                                    <div class="sitting-event-head">
                                        <span class="sitting-event-sequence">#@stored.SequenceNumber</span>
                                        <span class="sitting-event-type">@DescribeEventType(stored.EventType)</span>
                                        <span class="record-secondary">
                                            @stored.ActorName as @DescribeActorRole(stored.ActorRole) ·
                                            @RestaurantClock.DateAndTimeWithSeconds(stored.OccurredAt)
                                        </span>
                                    </div>

                                    @if (stored.Operations.Count == 0)
                                    {
                                        <p class="record-secondary">
                                            No operations recorded, which §6.5.1 forbids — worth reporting.
                                        </p>
                                    }
                                    else
                                    {
                                        <ul class="sitting-operations">
                                            @foreach (StoredOrderOperation operation in stored.Operations)
                                            {
                                                <li>@DescribeOperation(operation)</li>
                                            }
                                        </ul>
                                    }
                                </li>
                            }
                        </ol>
                    }
                </article>
            }
        }

        <p><a href="/administration/sittings">Back to sittings</a></p>
    </section>
}

@* Rules nobody else reads: this page's own totals, roster, tally and event stream. Everything it
   shares — the page head, the record list, the headings, the rules, the corrected total, the numeric
   treatment, the small forms — is app.css's §11.12 vocabulary and is not restated here (M6 Slice 34).
   App.razor links the static stylesheet rather than the scoped bundle, so component CSS isolation is
   not active; a page-local block is the arrangement, and re-declaring a shared name in one would win
   silently from later in the document, which is F-66. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>Somebody a correction can be billed to: a member, or anyone who already has an order here.</summary>
    private sealed record BillablePerson(Guid PersonIdentifier, string Name);

    /// <summary>
    /// The two things the one correction form can do. They are two different §6.2 event types with two
    /// different operation subtypes, so they cannot be one Save — but they are one form, because a
    /// per-line panel would need a distinct form name per row and static SSR has no model to bind
    /// a dynamic set of them to. This is the shape TableDisplays and CounterSitting already use: one
    /// picker, at the bottom, that can name any row above it.
    /// </summary>
    private const string AdjustAction = "adjust";

    private const string RemoveAction = "remove";

    private CounterSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingMemberSummary> _members = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingBillEntry> _bill = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> _lines = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingOrderRecord> _records = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _menu = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<BillablePerson> _peopleAtTheTable = [];
    private int _eventCount;

    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _rejectionReasons = [];

    /// <summary>The sitting this page reports on. Every query is scoped by it, never by the table.</summary>
    [Parameter]
    public Guid SittingId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "sitting-correct-line")]
    private CorrectLineInputModel CorrectInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "sitting-add-line")]
    private AddLineInputModel AddInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string RecordPath => $"/administration/sittings/{SittingId}";

    private string CounterPath => $"/counter/sittings/{SittingId}";

    private decimal TableTotal => _bill.Sum(entry => entry.PersonTotalAmount);

    /// <summary>The " · settled 9:14 PM by Cass" tail of the header line, built here because it reads as one sentence.</summary>
    private string SettledSuffix
    {
        get
        {
            if (_sitting is not { ClosedAt: { } closedAt })
            {
                return string.Empty;
            }

            string by = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_sitting.ClosedByName)
                ? string.Empty
                : $" by {_sitting.ClosedByName}";

            return $" · settled {RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(closedAt)}{by}";
        }
    }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so the defaults live here.
        CorrectInput ??= new();
        AddInput ??= new();

        await LoadAsync();

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            CorrectInput.Action = AdjustAction;
            AddInput.Quantity = 1;
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Everything the page shows, re-read in one pass. Small, indexed queries.</summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;

        _sitting = await CounterReads.GetSittingAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            _members = [];
            _bill = [];
            _lines = [];
            _records = [];
            _menu = [];
            _peopleAtTheTable = [];
            _eventCount = 0;
            return;
        }

        _members = await SittingDirectory.ListMembersAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _bill = await OrderReads.ListSittingBillAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _lines = await OrderReads.ListLinesForSittingAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _records = await SittingRecords.ListOrderRecordsForSittingAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _menu = await MenuItems.ListAsync(cancellationToken);

        _eventCount = _records.Sum(order => order.Events.Count);
        _peopleAtTheTable = BuildPeopleAtTheTable();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The roster, plus anybody who has an order without a membership row. The union rather than the
    /// roster alone, because the picker must never be unable to name somebody whose bill is on the screen
    /// directly above it.
    /// </summary>
    private IReadOnlyList<BillablePerson> BuildPeopleAtTheTable()
    {
        List<BillablePerson> people = _members
            .Select(member => new BillablePerson(member.PersonIdentifier, member.RosterName))
            .ToList();

        foreach (SittingBillEntry entry in _bill)
        {
            if (!people.Any(person => person.PersonIdentifier == entry.PersonIdentifier))
            {
                people.Add(new BillablePerson(entry.PersonIdentifier, entry.BillName));
            }
        }

        return people;
    }

    /// <summary>§6.7 through §6.5.8: an administrator's corrective price change or removal on a settled bill.</summary>
    private async Task CorrectLineAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(CorrectInput.OrderLineIdentifier, out Guid orderLineIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose which line to correct.";
            return;
        }

        OrderLineView? line = _lines
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.OrderLineIdentifier == orderLineIdentifier);

        if (line is null)
        {
            // Somebody corrected it between this page rendering and the button being pressed. Re-read and
            // say so rather than sending an operation the transaction would refuse anyway.
            _errorMessage = "That line is no longer on the bill. The record below has been refreshed.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        if (CorrectInput.Action == RemoveAction)
        {
            await AppendAsync(
                administrator,
                line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
                OrderEventType.StaffEdit,
                [new LineRemovedOperation(orderLineIdentifier, Blank(CorrectInput.Reason))],
                "line-removed");
            return;
        }

        if (CorrectInput.Action != AdjustAction)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose whether to change the price or take the line off the bill.";
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(CorrectInput.Reason))
        {
            _errorMessage = "A price change needs a reason — it is the sentence somebody reads back later.";
            return;
        }

        if (CorrectInput.NewUnitPriceAmount < 0m)
        {
            _errorMessage = "A price cannot be negative.";
            return;
        }

        // Rounded once, here, away from zero — matching numeric(10,2)'s own rule — so the operation row,
        // the projection, and the number reported back are the same value rather than three independent
        // roundings of the same input. The same decision MenuAdministration made for reprice.
        decimal newUnitPrice = Math.Round(CorrectInput.NewUnitPriceAmount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);

        await AppendAsync(
            administrator,
            line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.PriceAdjustment,
            [new LinePriceAdjustedOperation(orderLineIdentifier, newUnitPrice, CorrectInput.Reason.Trim())],
            "line-repriced");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.7's other half: a plate that went out and was never billed. Routed through the living-order path
    /// so it works for somebody who joined and never sent anything — their order row is created inside the
    /// same transaction (§6.1), which is not something this surface can do for itself.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task AddLineAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(AddInput.PersonIdentifier, out Guid personIdentifier)
            || _peopleAtTheTable.All(person => person.PersonIdentifier != personIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose which guest this line belongs to.";
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(AddInput.MenuItemIdentifier, out Guid menuItemIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose an item to add.";
            return;
        }

        MenuItemSummary? item = _menu
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.MenuItemIdentifier == menuItemIdentifier);

        if (item is null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That item is no longer on the menu.";
            return;
        }

        // §7 keeps a deactivated item visible and unorderable; the transaction re-checks the flag under
        // its own lock (§6.5.4), so this only makes the answer immediate.
        if (!item.IsActive)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                $"{item.Name} is currently marked unavailable, so it cannot be added. Make it available first.";
            return;
        }

        if (AddInput.Quantity is < 1 or > 100)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Quantity must be between 1 and 100.";
            return;
        }

        // The line's own identity, UUIDv7 like every other key (ADR-0011). The unit price passed here is
        // ignored: the transaction prices the line from the menu row it reads under the lock (§6.5.4).
        LineAddedOperation added = new(
            Identifiers.Create(),
            menuItemIdentifier,
            AddInput.Quantity,
            item.PriceAmount,
            Blank(AddInput.Note));

        AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventToLivingOrderAsync(
            SittingId,
            personIdentifier,
            new ProposedOrderEvent(
                OrderEventType.StaffEdit,
                administrator,
                OrderActorRole.Administrator,
                [added]),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        await ReportAsync(result, "line-added");
    }

    private async Task AppendAsync(
        Guid administrator,
        Guid guestOrderIdentifier,
        OrderEventType eventType,
        IReadOnlyList<OrderOperation> operations,
        string outcome)
    {
        AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventAsync(
            guestOrderIdentifier,
            new ProposedOrderEvent(eventType, administrator, OrderActorRole.Administrator, operations),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        await ReportAsync(result, outcome);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Redirect on success so a refresh cannot re-append; render the refusal in place on failure, because
    /// the per-operation reasons §6.5.9 produces do not survive a query string and are the whole value of
    /// the message.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task ReportAsync(AppendOrderEventResult result, string outcome)
    {
        if (result.IsAppended)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo($"{RecordPath}?done={outcome}");
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage = DescribeRefusal(result);
        _rejectionReasons = result.Errors.Select(error => error.Reason).ToArray();
        await LoadAsync();
    }

    private static string DescribeRefusal(AppendOrderEventResult result) => result.Outcome switch
    {
        AppendOrderEventOutcome.SittingNotFound => "That sitting no longer exists. Nothing was written.",
        AppendOrderEventOutcome.OrderNotFound => "There is no order here to append to. Nothing was written.",
        _ => "Nothing was written. The record below has been refreshed.",
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The sitting must still exist and the acting administrator must be identifiable —
    /// <c>order_event.actor_person_identifier</c> is NOT NULL and §6.2 requires every event to name
    /// somebody. Endpoint authorization already guarantees the second; this is the belt to that brace.
    /// Also refuses on an open sitting, which the markup does not offer but a replayed post could.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryBegin(out Guid administrator)
    {
        administrator = Guid.Empty;

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/sittings");
            return false;
        }

        if (_sitting.IsOpen)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                "This table is still open, so there is nothing to correct. Settle it at the counter first.";
            return false;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } identifier)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return false;
        }

        administrator = identifier;
        return true;
    }

    private bool HasAnOrder(Guid personIdentifier)
        => _bill.Any(entry => entry.PersonIdentifier == personIdentifier);

    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> LinesFor(Guid guestOrderIdentifier)
        => _lines.Where(line => line.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier).ToArray();

    private string LineOptionLabel(OrderLineView line)
        => $"{OwnerNameFor(line.GuestOrderIdentifier)} — {line.Quantity} × {line.MenuItemName} " +
           $"at {Money(line.CurrentUnitPriceAmount)}";

    private string OwnerNameFor(Guid guestOrderIdentifier)
    {
        SittingBillEntry? entry = _bill
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier);

        if (entry is not null)
        {
            return entry.BillName;
        }

        SittingOrderRecord? orderRecord = _records
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier);

        return orderRecord?.OwnerName ?? "Unknown guest";
    }

    private string ItemOptionLabel(MenuItemSummary item)
        => item.IsActive
            ? $"{item.Name} — {Money(item.PriceAmount)}"
            : $"{item.Name} — {Money(item.PriceAmount)} (currently unavailable)";

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the five <c>order_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits, falling
    /// back to the stored string for anything else. The words are spelled out here rather than taken from
    /// <c>OrderEventVocabulary</c>, which is internal to the data-access assembly on purpose — a display
    /// label is not the writer's business, and a reader that threw on an unrecognised word would blank the
    /// one page whose job is to show what is actually stored. Same shape as ManageMenuItem's.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "guest_submission" => "Guest send",
        "staff_edit" => "Staff edit",
        "price_adjustment" => "Price change",
        "fulfillment" => "Delivered",
        "fulfillment_reversal" => "Delivery undone",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The four <c>order_event.actor_role</c> values, on the same terms. <c>guest</c> is a capacity rather
    /// than a stored role (§0, §3.7) — an administrator eating lunch appears here as a guest, and that is
    /// correct.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeActorRole(string actorRole) => actorRole switch
    {
        "guest" => "a guest",
        "kitchen" => "the kitchen",
        "counter" => "the counter",
        "administrator" => "an administrator",
        _ => actorRole,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// One stored operation in a sentence. The five kinds are the discriminators the reader's UNION
    /// projects; an unknown one renders as itself beside the line it names, so nothing is ever swallowed.
    /// </summary>
    private string DescribeOperation(StoredOrderOperation operation) => operation.OperationKind switch
    {
        "line_added" =>
            $"Added {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} at " +
            $"{Money(operation.UnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{NoteSuffix(operation.CustomizationNote)}",
        "line_removed" =>
            $"Removed {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_price_adjusted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} repriced to " +
            $"{Money(operation.NewUnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_fulfilled" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} delivered",
        "line_fulfillment_reverted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} put back with the kitchen",
        _ => $"{operation.OperationKind} on {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}",
    };

    private static string NoteSuffix(string? note)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(note) ? string.Empty : $" — “{note.Trim()}”";

    private static string ReasonSuffix(string? reason)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(reason) ? string.Empty : $" — {reason.Trim()}";

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "line-repriced" =>
            "Price changed. The settled total above is unchanged — the correction shows beside it.",
        "line-removed" =>
            "Line taken off the bill. It stays in the record with your name and the reason; it simply stops being charged.",
        "line-added" =>
            "Line added. It appears in the corrected total, not in the settled one, which is never rewritten.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private static string? Blank(string? value)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value) ? null : value.Trim();

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    private sealed class CorrectLineInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose which line to correct.")]
        public string OrderLineIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose what to do.")]
        public string Action { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Range(0, 99999999.99, ErrorMessage = "The price must be between 0 and 99,999,999.99.")]
        public decimal NewUnitPriceAmount { get; set; }

        [StringLength(200, ErrorMessage = "A reason must be 200 characters or fewer.")]
        public string? Reason { get; set; }
    }

    private sealed class AddLineInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose which guest this line belongs to.")]
        public string PersonIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose an item to add.")]
        public string MenuItemIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Range(1, 100, ErrorMessage = "Quantity must be between 1 and 100.")]
        public int Quantity { get; set; } = 1;

        [StringLength(500, ErrorMessage = "A note must be 500 characters or fewer.")]
        public string? Note { get; set; }
    }
}

@* This page declares nothing. Its facts grid, its headings, its rules, its small forms, its chips
   and its back link are all app.css's §11.12 vocabulary — four pages each carried an inline copy of
   that vocabulary until M6 Slice 34, and the copies had drifted (F-66). A page may still keep a block
