@code {
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-rename")]
    private RenameInputModel RenameInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/tables/{TableId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds RenameInput itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        RenameInput ??= new();

        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_table is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        // On GET, pre-fill the rename box with the current label and render any post/redirect flash.
        // On POST the submitted value is already bound, so it must not be overwritten.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RenameInput.Label))
            {
                RenameInput.Label = _table.Label;
            }

            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task RenameAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        RenameTableOutcome outcome = await Tables.RenameTableAsync(
            TableId, RenameInput.Label.Trim(), HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RenameTableOutcome.Renamed:
                RedirectWithOutcome("renamed");
                break;
            case RenameTableOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("rename-no-change");
                break;
            case RenameTableOutcome.LabelTaken:
                _errorMessage = "Another table already uses that label. Please choose a different one.";
                break;
            case RenameTableOutcome.TableNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RotateSecretAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        RotateJoinSecretOutcome outcome = await Tables.RotateJoinSecretAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RotateJoinSecretOutcome.Rotated:
                RedirectWithOutcome("secret-rotated");
                break;
            case RotateJoinSecretOutcome.TableNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ToggleActivationAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_table.IsActive;
        TableActivationOutcome outcome = await Tables.SetTableActiveAsync(TableId, target, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case TableActivationOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "reactivated" : "deactivated");
                break;
            case TableActivationOutcome.NoChange:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case TableActivationOutcome.TableNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
                break;
        }
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "renamed" => "Table renamed.",
        "rename-no-change" => "That was already the label — nothing changed.",
        "secret-rotated" => "Join secret rotated. Every outstanding QR for this table has stopped working; "
            + "paired displays pick up the new one automatically.",
        "deactivated" => "Table deactivated. Its join tokens no longer validate and its display stops rendering.",
        "reactivated" => "Table reactivated.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private sealed class RenameInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a label.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The label must be 1–64 characters.")]
        public string Label { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

   Static SSR, like every administration surface.

   Generate deliberately does NOT post/redirect/get: the plaintext code exists exactly once, in the
   response to the POST that made it, and a redirect would throw it away — the same reason the TOTP
   slice renders recovery codes in place. A refresh therefore mints a fresh code; the previous one is
   simply left to expire, which is harmless because codes are single-use and short-lived.

   Revoke does use post/redirect/get, and picks its device from a select rather than rendering a form
   per row — the same shape ManagePerson uses for role revocation, and the reason is the same: one
   named form per action keeps static-SSR form matching unambiguous.

   §11.12 vocabulary throughout and no inline copy of any of it (M6 Slice 34). The roster is a shared
   `.record-list`, so below the breakpoint each display is a card whose cells state their own labels;
   the small forms and the facts are the shared `.manage-*` detail vocabulary. What this page used to
   declare inline was the retired per-page table wrapper, a second chip set pinned to literals off the
   palette, a
   `.visually-hidden` still using the deprecated `clip`, and a `.manage-inline-form select` with no
   touch-target height at all — which is F-66, and the whole of it is now read from app.css.

   Generating a code is the thing an administrator opens this page to do, so it is the page head's own
   action rather than a form further down. That also puts it where §16.3 scenario 16 measures it: this
   surface is in the barrier as of Slice 34, and with no display ever paired the generate button is the

   arrangement here and why re-declaring a shared name in one would silently win. *@
<style>
    .pairing-issued {
        margin: 1rem 0;
        padding: 1rem;
        border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
        border-radius: 0.6rem;
        background-color: var(--surface);
        text-align: center;
    }

    .pairing-issued-label {
        margin: 0;
        font-size: 0.85rem;
        color: var(--ink-soft);
    }

    .pairing-code {
        margin: 0.35rem 0 0.5rem;
        font-family: var(--font-monospace);
        font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 6vw, 2.5rem);
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: 0.22em;
    }
</style>

@code {
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private IReadOnlyList<TableDisplayDeviceSummary> _devices = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<TableDisplayDeviceSummary> _revocableDevices = [];
    private string? _issuedCode;
    private DateTimeOffset? _issuedExpiresAt;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "display-revoke")]
    private RevokeInputModel RevokeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/tables/{TableId}";

    private string DisplaysPath => $"/administration/tables/{TableId}/displays";

    /// <summary>The absolute URL to read aloud to whoever is holding the tablet (§4.2).</summary>
    private string PairingUrl => $"{Options.PublicOrigin.TrimEnd('/')}{DisplayRoutes.Pair}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds RevokeInput itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        RevokeInput ??= new();

        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_table is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        await LoadDevicesAsync();

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadDevicesAsync()
    {
        _devices = await DisplayDevices.ListDevicesForTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        _revocableDevices = _devices.Where(device => !device.IsRevoked).ToArray();
    }

    private async Task GenerateCodeAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that
            // brace, because created_by_person_identifier is NOT NULL and has no anonymous option.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        IssuePairingCodeResult result = await Pairing.IssuePairingCodeAsync(
            TableId,
            administrator,
            TimeSpan.FromMinutes(Options.TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == IssuePairingCodeOutcome.Issued)
        {
            // Rendered in place, never redirected: this is the only moment the plaintext exists.
            _issuedCode = result.Code;
            _issuedExpiresAt = result.ExpiresAt;
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage = "This table is deactivated, so it cannot take a new display. Reactivate it first.";
    }

    private async Task RevokeDeviceAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        // Bound as text rather than Guid so the "Choose a display…" empty option is representable and
        // InputSelect never has to parse a non-string type.
        if (!Guid.TryParse(RevokeInput.DeviceIdentifier, out Guid deviceIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose which display to revoke.";
            return;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome outcome = await Pairing.RevokeDeviceAsync(
            deviceIdentifier, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome.Revoked:
                Navigation.NavigateTo($"{DisplaysPath}?done=revoked");
                break;
            case RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome.AlreadyRevoked:
                Navigation.NavigateTo($"{DisplaysPath}?done=already-revoked");
                break;
            case RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome.DeviceNotFound:
                _errorMessage = "That display no longer exists.";
                await LoadDevicesAsync();
                break;
        }
    }

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "revoked" => "Display revoked. Its credential stops working on the device's next request.",
        "already-revoked" => "That display had already been revoked — nothing changed.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private sealed class RevokeInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose which display to revoke.")]
        public string DeviceIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How far back "settled today" reaches. Long enough to cover a whole service and the shift change
    /// either side of it, short enough that this stays a working list rather than an archive — the
    /// archive is administration's (§11.4). Not configuration: §13 does not name it, and a setting
    /// nobody would change is only another way to be wrong.
    /// </summary>
    private static readonly TimeSpan RecentlySettledWindow = TimeSpan.FromHours(12);

    /// <summary>A hard cap alongside the window, so one absurd day cannot render a thousand rows.</summary>
    private const int RecentlySettledLimit = 25;

    // Captured once, so nothing touches _lifetime.Token after Dispose — the shape KitchenBoard,
    // TableDisplay, and TableOrderSurface all use.
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _lifetime = new();
    private CancellationToken _stopping;
    private IDisposable? _subscription;
    private bool _disposed;

    private bool _loaded;
    private IReadOnlyList<CounterSittingSummary> _openSittings = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<CounterSittingSummary> _recentlySettled = [];

    private decimal _openTotal;
    private int _openPendingLines;

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether a circuit produced this markup, published as an attribute — §11.10's first bit, which
    /// every interactive surface publishes: <c>KitchenBoard</c>, <c>CounterSitting</c>,
    /// <c>TableOrderSurface</c>, <c>TableDisplay</c> and <c>TableArea</c>.
    ///
    /// <para>This board is the one screen in the application whose entire purpose is a number that
    /// moves while somebody stands reading it (§11.3, §9). A prerendered copy of it is correct as of the
    /// request and then correct forever, which is the failure mode that looks most like success — so
    /// "a circuit is behind this" has to be assertable from outside.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><b>The sentence that used to end this paragraph was wrong, and its wrongness is F-47.</b>
    /// It read "until now it was the only one of the five live surfaces that did not say". There is no
    /// list of five. <c>App.razor</c>'s <c>RenderModeForPage</c> makes <em>every</em> routable page
    /// interactive unless it carries <c>[ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]</c>, which is six pages plus the
    /// island hosted inside <c>/table/{id}</c> — and <c>/table</c> had been one of them since M3 while
    /// publishing nothing at all. A rule enforced as a list of examples is enforced as a list of
    /// examples (F-46); §11.10 states the rule and §16.4's contract test derives the set from the
    /// attribute rather than from anybody's memory.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string IsLiveAttributeValue => RendererInfo.IsInteractive ? "true" : "false";

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether <see cref="LoadAsync"/> has answered, published alongside <c>data-live</c> — §11.10's
    /// second bit.
    ///
    /// <para><b>Why both, rather than either.</b> <c>ComponentBase</c> renders the moment
    /// <c>OnInitializedAsync</c> yields, so the circuit's first render is <c>data-live="true"</c> with
    /// <c>_loaded</c> still false — the one state in which neither the open-sittings list nor "Settled
    /// today" is in the document. A reader that waited on <c>data-live</c> alone would be steered
    /// <em>towards</em> that instant rather than past it, and would see two empty lists and believe
    /// them.</para>
    ///
    /// <para>The window is real rather than theoretical, and it is not the prerender: prerendering runs
    /// the whole lifecycle before it emits, so the first HTML a browser gets is fully loaded. It is the
    /// hand-over. The circuit builds this component again from nothing, and the DOM goes back to
    /// "Loading the floor…" for as long as two queries take — milliseconds on a workstation, long
    /// enough on a loaded CI runner for §16.3 scenario 10 to read the board mid-reload and find a
    /// settled table on neither list (F-44).</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string IsLoadedAttributeValue => _loaded ? "true" : "false";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _stopping = _lifetime.Token;
        await LoadAsync();
        _loaded = true;
    }

    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            // Only on the circuit: OnAfterRender does not run during prerendering, so no subscription is
            // created for a render about to be thrown away.
            _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Both queries, one pass. Small and indexed; a counter is not a hot path.</summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        _openSittings = await CounterReads.ListOpenSittingsAsync(_stopping);

        _recentlySettled = await CounterReads.ListRecentlyClosedSittingsAsync(
            Clock.UtcNow - RecentlySettledWindow,
            RecentlySettledLimit,
            _stopping);

        _openTotal = _openSittings.Sum(sitting => sitting.CurrentTotalAmount);
        _openPendingLines = _openSittings.Sum(sitting => sitting.PendingLineCount);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §9 lists the counter as a consumer of OrderLinesChanged; a close and a join both change what this
    /// list says too, so all four are handled with one re-read. Nothing is filtered by identifier: this
    /// board is the whole floor by definition, so every one of these events is its business.
    /// </summary>
    private void OnDomainNotification(DomainNotification notification)
    {
        bool concernsTheFloor = notification
            is OrderLinesChanged
            or LineFulfillmentChanged
            or SittingClosed
            or SittingMemberJoined;

        if (!concernsTheFloor)
        {
            return;
        }

        _ = InvokeAsync(async () =>
        {
            if (_disposed)
            {
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                await LoadAsync();
                StateHasChanged();
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Disposed between the broadcast and the query; nothing to update.
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                // Same, one layer down.
            }
        });
    }

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    private static string SittingPath(Guid sittingIdentifier) => $"/counter/sittings/{sittingIdentifier}";

    private static string JoinCodePath(Guid tableIdentifier) => $"/counter/tables/{tableIdentifier}/join-code";

    /// <summary>
    /// How long a table has been sitting, rendered coarsely — a duration, not an instant, so it does not
    /// go through <see cref="RestaurantTime"/>: there is no zone to render an elapsed span in.
    /// </summary>
    private string Elapsed(DateTimeOffset since)
    {
        TimeSpan elapsed = Clock.UtcNow - since;

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.Zero)
        {
            elapsed = TimeSpan.Zero;
        }

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1))
        {
            return "under a minute";
        }

        int minutes = (int)elapsed.TotalMinutes;
        if (minutes < 60)
        {
            return $"{minutes}m";
        }

        int hours = minutes / 60;
        return $"{hours}h {minutes % 60:D2}m";
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _disposed = true;
        _subscription?.Dispose();
        _lifetime.Cancel();
        _lifetime.Dispose();
    }
}

@* The counter's join-code fallback (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.5, §11.3: "a per-table 'Show join code'
   button rendering the rotating QR full-screen").

   The same server-rendered rotating QR the table's own display shows, on a screen a guest can be walked
   to when that display is dead. The join secret never leaves the server — this page carries only the
   rendered SVG and the URL it encodes (§4.1, §4.5).

   Deliberately the same shape as the administration page at
   /administration/tables/{id}/join-code rather than a shared component: the two differ in their policy
   (§3.7 gives the counter its own), in where "back" goes, and in how big the code is drawn — a counter
   holds this up across a pass, an administrator reads it at a desk. What they must not differ in is the
   code itself, and they do not: both call ITableJoinTokens.DescribeCurrentAsync and render what it
   returns.

   Static SSR, so this is a snapshot of the current window. That is safe by construction: a scanned code
   keeps working for the current *and* previous window (worst case about twice the rotation, §4.3), so it
   cannot die in a guest's hand mid-scan, and "Show a fresh code" re-renders on demand. The
   window-aligned automatic refresh belongs to the paired display surface (§11.5), which has a circuit to
   run a timer on. A deactivated or unknown table renders no code (§4.1). *@

<PageTitle>@(_table is null ? "Join code" : $"Join code — {_table.Label}")</PageTitle>

@code {
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private TableJoinQrCode? _qr;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    private string JoinCodePath => $"/counter/tables/{TableId}/join-code";

    private int SecondsUntilRotation => _qr is null
        ? 0
        : Math.Max(0, (int)Math.Ceiling((_qr.NextRotationAt - _qr.GeneratedAt).TotalSeconds));

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (_table is null || !_table.IsActive)
        {
            return;
        }

        _qr = await JoinTokens.DescribeCurrentAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
    }
}

</section>

@code {
    /// <summary>Somebody the counter can put a line against: a member, or anyone who already has an order.</summary>
    private sealed record BillablePerson(Guid PersonIdentifier, string Name);

    // Captured once, so nothing touches _lifetime.Token after Dispose.
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _lifetime = new();
    private CancellationToken _stopping;
    private IDisposable? _subscription;
    private bool _disposed;

    private Guid? _person;
    private OrderActorRole _actorRole = OrderActorRole.Counter;
    private bool _loaded;
    private bool _busy;

    private CounterSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingBillEntry> _bill = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> _lines = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingMemberSummary> _members = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _menu = [];

    private string? _notice;
    private string? _problem;
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _rejectionReasons = [];

    private Guid? _adjustingLine;
    private string _adjustPriceText = string.Empty;
    private string _adjustReason = string.Empty;

    private Guid? _removingLine;
    private string _removeReason = string.Empty;

    private string _addPersonText = string.Empty;
    private string _addMenuItemText = string.Empty;
    private int _addQuantity = 1;
    private string _addNote = string.Empty;

    private bool _confirmingClose;

    /// <summary>The sitting this screen bills. Every query is scoped by it, never by the table.</summary>
    [Parameter]
    [EditorRequired]
    public Guid SittingId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    private decimal TableTotal => _bill.Sum(entry => entry.PersonTotalAmount);

    /// <summary>
    /// People who joined the sitting (§5.1) but have no living order yet (§6.1) — and so no
    /// <c>sitting_bill</c> row, because that view is built from <c>guest_order</c>.
    /// </summary>
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingMemberSummary> MembersWithoutAnOrder
        => _members
            .Where(member => !_bill.Any(entry => entry.PersonIdentifier == member.PersonIdentifier))
            .ToArray();

    /// <summary>
    /// Everyone a line can be added for: the roster, plus anyone who somehow has an order without a
    /// membership row. The union rather than the roster alone, because the picker must never be unable
    /// to name somebody whose bill is on the screen directly above it.
    /// </summary>
    private IReadOnlyList<BillablePerson> PeopleAtTheTable
    {
        get
        {
            List<BillablePerson> people = _members
                .Select(member => new BillablePerson(member.PersonIdentifier, member.RosterName))
                .ToList();

            foreach (SittingBillEntry entry in _bill)
            {
                if (!people.Any(person => person.PersonIdentifier == entry.PersonIdentifier))
                {
                    people.Add(new BillablePerson(entry.PersonIdentifier, entry.BillName));
                }
            }

            return people;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The " · settled 3:04 PM by Cass" tail of the header line, built here rather than as nested
    /// conditionals in the markup — it is one sentence, and it reads like one in the source too.
    /// </summary>
    private string SettledSuffix
    {
        get
        {
            if (_sitting is not { ClosedAt: { } closedAt })
            {
                return string.Empty;
            }

            string by = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_sitting.ClosedByName)
                ? string.Empty
                : $" by {_sitting.ClosedByName}";

            return $" · settled {RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(closedAt)}{by}";
        }
    }

    private string JoinCodePath
        => _sitting is null ? "/counter" : $"/counter/tables/{_sitting.TableIdentifier}/join-code";

    /// <summary>
    /// <c>"true"</c> when a circuit rendered this markup, <c>"false"</c> during the prerender pass. The
    /// same attribute, for the same reason, as <c>KitchenBoard</c>'s and <c>TableOrderSurface</c>'s.
    ///
    /// <para>A prerendered till is the dangerous kind of broken, because it is the kind that looks
    /// right: the bill is correct as of the request, every total adds up, and Adjust price, Remove, Add
    /// to the bill and Close &amp; settle are all <c>@onclick</c> handlers with no circuit behind them.
    /// Pressing any of them does nothing at all — no refusal, no flash, no error — and the screen also
    /// never hears §9, so a guest sending while somebody stands at the till changes nothing on it. The
    /// attribute costs eight characters and turns that into something an operator can see in dev tools
    /// and a scenario can name in one sentence.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string IsLiveAttributeValue => RendererInfo.IsInteractive ? "true" : "false";

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether <see cref="LoadAsync"/> has answered, published alongside <c>data-live</c> — §11.10's
    /// second bit, and the half this surface was missing until M6 Slice 23.
    ///
    /// <para>The circuit's first render is <c>data-live="true"</c> with <c>_loaded</c> still false, and
    /// this page renders <c>&lt;h1&gt;Loading…&lt;/h1&gt;</c> in that state — no bill, no totals, no
    /// controls. Waiting on <c>data-live</c> alone is therefore a wait that lands on the one render
    /// where none of the things a caller came for exist. That is worse than harmless here, because the
    /// state immediately below it in the markup is <em>"Sitting not found"</em>: a reader that arrived
    /// early and asked what the page says would be told the identifier is stale.</para>
    ///
    /// <para>Not the prerender — that emits fully loaded markup. The hand-over, where the component is
    /// rebuilt from nothing and the DOM returns to loading for as long as the reads take (F-44).</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string IsLoadedAttributeValue => _loaded ? "true" : "false";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _stopping = _lifetime.Token;

        if (AuthenticationStateTask is not null)
        {
            AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;
            _person = PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(state.User);

            // §6.2: a staff_edit or price_adjustment may be authored by counter or administrator.
            // Record what the person actually is — counter wins when they hold both, because that is
            // the capacity they are standing at this screen in.
            _actorRole = state.User.IsInRole(RestaurantRoles.Counter)
                ? OrderActorRole.Counter
                : OrderActorRole.Administrator;
        }

        await LoadAsync();
        _loaded = true;
    }

    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            // Only on the circuit: OnAfterRender does not run during prerendering, so no subscription is
            // created for a render about to be thrown away.
            _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Everything the screen shows, re-read in one pass. Small, indexed queries.</summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        _sitting = await CounterReads.GetSittingAsync(SittingId, _stopping);

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            _bill = [];
            _lines = [];
            _members = [];
            return;
        }

        _bill = await OrderReads.ListSittingBillAsync(SittingId, _stopping);
        _lines = await OrderReads.ListLinesForSittingAsync(SittingId, _stopping);
        _members = await SittingDirectory.ListMembersAsync(SittingId, _stopping);
        _menu = await MenuDirectory.ListAsync(_stopping);
    }

    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> LinesFor(Guid guestOrderIdentifier)
        => _lines.Where(line => line.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier).ToArray();

    private string ItemOptionLabel(MenuItemSummary item)
        => item.IsActive
            ? $"{item.Name} — {Money(item.PriceAmount)}"
            : $"{item.Name} — {Money(item.PriceAmount)} (currently unavailable)";

    private void StartAdjust(OrderLineView line)
    {
        CancelEditors();
        _adjustingLine = line.OrderLineIdentifier;
        _adjustPriceText = line.CurrentUnitPriceAmount.ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        _adjustReason = string.Empty;
    }

    private void StartRemove(OrderLineView line)
    {
        CancelEditors();
        _removingLine = line.OrderLineIdentifier;
        _removeReason = string.Empty;
    }

    private void CancelEditors()
    {
        _adjustingLine = null;
        _removingLine = null;
        _confirmingClose = false;
    }

    private void BeginClose()
    {
        CancelEditors();
        _confirmingClose = true;
    }

    private void AbandonClose()
    {
        _confirmingClose = false;
    }

    /// <summary>§11.3: "price adjustment dialog (new price + required reason)".</summary>
    private async Task AdjustPriceAsync(OrderLineView line)
    {
        ClearMessages();

        // Parsed invariantly for the reason MoneyText formats invariantly: the amount is a
        // numeric(10,2), and which separator the container's locale happens to use is not a decision
        // anybody made about this restaurant.
        if (!decimal.TryParse(
                _adjustPriceText,
                NumberStyles.Number,
                CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
                out decimal newUnitPrice)
            || newUnitPrice < 0m)
        {
            _problem = "Enter the new unit price as a plain number, for example 12.50.";
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_adjustReason))
        {
            _problem = "A price adjustment needs a reason — it is shown beside the change on the bill.";
            return;
        }

        newUnitPrice = Math.Round(newUnitPrice, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);

        bool appended = await AppendToOrderAsync(
            line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.PriceAdjustment,
            [new LinePriceAdjustedOperation(line.OrderLineIdentifier, newUnitPrice, _adjustReason.Trim())],
            $"{line.MenuItemName} is now {Money(newUnitPrice)} each.");

        if (appended)
        {
            CancelEditors();
        }
    }

    /// <summary>§11.3: "add/remove line (staff edit, optional reason on removal)".</summary>
    private async Task RemoveLineAsync(OrderLineView line)
    {
        bool appended = await AppendToOrderAsync(
            line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.StaffEdit,
            [new LineRemovedOperation(line.OrderLineIdentifier, Blank(_removeReason))],
            $"{line.Quantity} × {line.MenuItemName} is off the bill.");

        if (appended)
        {
            CancelEditors();
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §11.3's staff add, through the living-order path so it works for a member who has never sent
    /// anything — their order is created inside the same transaction (§6.1).
    /// </summary>
    private async Task AddLineAsync()
    {
        ClearMessages();

        if (!Guid.TryParse(_addPersonText, out Guid personIdentifier))
        {
            _problem = "Choose which guest this is for.";
            return;
        }

        BillablePerson? recipient = PeopleAtTheTable
            .FirstOrDefault(person => person.PersonIdentifier == personIdentifier);

        if (recipient is null)
        {
            _problem = "That guest is no longer at this table.";
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(_addMenuItemText, out Guid menuItemIdentifier))
        {
            _problem = "Choose an item to add.";
            return;
        }

        MenuItemSummary? item = _menu
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.MenuItemIdentifier == menuItemIdentifier);

        if (item is null)
        {
            _problem = "That item is no longer on the menu.";
            return;
        }

        // §7 keeps a deactivated item visible and unorderable; the transaction re-checks the flag under
        // its own lock (§6.5.4), so this only makes the answer immediate.
        if (!item.IsActive)
        {
            _problem = $"{item.Name} is currently unavailable, so it cannot be added.";
            return;
        }

        if (_addQuantity is < 1 or > 100)
        {
            _problem = "Quantity must be between 1 and 100.";
            return;
        }

        // The line's own identity, UUIDv7 like every other key (ADR-0011). The unit price sent here is
        // ignored: the transaction prices the line from the menu row it reads under the lock (§6.5.4).
        LineAddedOperation added = new(
            Identifiers.Create(),
            menuItemIdentifier,
            _addQuantity,
            item.PriceAmount,
            Blank(_addNote));

        bool appended = await AppendToLivingOrderAsync(
            personIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.StaffEdit,
            [added],
            $"{_addQuantity} × {item.Name} added to {recipient.Name}'s order.");

        if (appended)
        {
            _addMenuItemText = string.Empty;
            _addQuantity = 1;
            _addNote = string.Empty;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>§5.3, through the workflow so the close is counted (§12) and announced (§9).</summary>
    private async Task CloseAndSettleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is not { } person || _busy)
        {
            return;
        }

        _busy = true;
        ClearMessages();

        try
        {
            CloseSittingResult result = await Settlement.CloseAndSettleAsync(SittingId, person, _stopping);

            _confirmingClose = false;

            switch (result.Outcome)
            {
                case CloseSittingOutcome.Closed when result.PendingLineCountAtClose > 0:
                    _notice =
                        $"Settled at {Money(result.SettledTotalAmount ?? 0m)} — with " +
                        $"{result.PendingLineCountAtClose} " +
                        $"{(result.PendingLineCountAtClose == 1 ? "line" : "lines")} still with the kitchen.";
                    break;

                case CloseSittingOutcome.Closed:
                    _notice = $"Settled at {Money(result.SettledTotalAmount ?? 0m)}.";
                    break;

                case CloseSittingOutcome.AlreadyClosed:
                    _notice = $"This table had already been settled at {Money(result.SettledTotalAmount ?? 0m)}.";
                    break;

                default:
                    _problem = "That sitting no longer exists.";
                    break;
            }

            await LoadAsync();
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            // The circuit went away mid-write. The transaction either committed or did not; either way
            // there is nobody left to tell.
        }
        finally
        {
            _busy = false;
        }
    }

    private async Task<bool> AppendToOrderAsync(
        Guid guestOrderIdentifier,
        OrderEventType eventType,
        IReadOnlyList<OrderOperation> operations,
        string successMessage)
    {
        if (_person is not { } person || _busy)
        {
            return false;
        }

        _busy = true;
        ClearMessages();

        try
        {
            AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventAsync(
                guestOrderIdentifier,
                new ProposedOrderEvent(eventType, person, _actorRole, operations),
                _stopping);

            return await ReportAsync(result, successMessage);
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            return false;
        }
        finally
        {
            _busy = false;
        }
    }

    private async Task<bool> AppendToLivingOrderAsync(
        Guid orderOwnerPersonIdentifier,
        OrderEventType eventType,
        IReadOnlyList<OrderOperation> operations,
        string successMessage)
    {
        if (_person is not { } person || _busy)
        {
            return false;
        }

        _busy = true;

        try
        {
            AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventToLivingOrderAsync(
                SittingId,
                orderOwnerPersonIdentifier,
                new ProposedOrderEvent(eventType, person, _actorRole, operations),
                _stopping);

            return await ReportAsync(result, successMessage);
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            return false;
        }
        finally
        {
            _busy = false;
        }
    }

    private async Task<bool> ReportAsync(AppendOrderEventResult result, string successMessage)
    {
        if (result.IsAppended)
        {
            _notice = successMessage;
        }
        else
        {
            _problem = DescribeRefusal(result);
            _rejectionReasons = result.Errors.Select(error => error.Reason).ToArray();
        }

        await LoadAsync();
        return result.IsAppended;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// A refusal in plain words. The likely causes here are races — a guest sending, the kitchen
    /// fulfilling, or somebody else closing a second earlier — so the message says what happened rather
    /// than reading like a fault, and the bill has already been refreshed by the time it is shown.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeRefusal(AppendOrderEventResult result)
    {
        if (result.Outcome is AppendOrderEventOutcome.SittingNotFound)
        {
            return "That sitting no longer exists. Nothing was changed.";
        }

        if (result.Outcome is AppendOrderEventOutcome.OrderNotFound)
        {
            return "There is no order to change here — the table may have been settled. Nothing was changed.";
        }

        return "Nothing was changed. The bill below has been refreshed.";
    }

    private void ClearMessages()
    {
        _notice = null;
        _problem = null;
        _rejectionReasons = [];
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §9 scopes every relevant notification by sitting, so this filters rather than re-reading on every
    /// event anywhere in the restaurant. <c>MenuChanged</c> is unscoped by construction and matters here
    /// because the add-an-item picker lists the menu (§7).
    /// </summary>
    private void OnDomainNotification(DomainNotification notification)
    {
        bool concernsThisSitting = notification switch
        {
            OrderLinesChanged changed => changed.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            LineFulfillmentChanged fulfilled => fulfilled.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            SittingMemberJoined joined => joined.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            SittingClosed closed => closed.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            MenuChanged => true,
            _ => false,
        };

        if (!concernsThisSitting)
        {
            return;
        }

        _ = InvokeAsync(async () =>
        {
            if (_disposed)
            {
                return;
            }

            try
            {
                await LoadAsync();
                StateHasChanged();
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Disposed between the broadcast and the query; nothing to update.
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                // Same, one layer down.
            }
        });
    }

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    private static string? Blank(string? value)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value) ? null : value.Trim();

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _disposed = true;
        _subscription?.Dispose();
        _lifetime.Cancel();
        _lifetime.Dispose();
    }
}

@page "/display/pair"
@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Displays
@using MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Displays
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [EnableRateLimiting(DisplayRoutes.PairingRateLimitPolicy)]
@layout DisplayLayout
@inject IDisplayDevicePairing Pairing
@inject RestaurantOptions Options
@inject NavigationManager Navigation

@* Display-device pairing (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.2, §11.5).

   Anonymous by necessity: this is the one page an unpaired screen can reach, and it is what it reaches
   INSTEAD of a sign-in page — a tablet has no account and never will. §4.2 pays for that openness with a
   rate limit rather than a credential: 5 attempts per minute per IP, enforced by the policy named in the
   attribute above, so an attacker cannot walk the 31^8 code space and a fat-fingered member of staff is
   barely inconvenienced.

   Static SSR, like every surface that writes a cookie: pairing's last act is to set the year-long device
   credential, which a Blazor circuit cannot do.

   Three entry states, decided on GET:
     • already paired  — the middleware resolved a live credential; offer the display, do not re-pair.
     • disconnected    — a cookie was presented but not honoured, so the middleware cleared it. §11.5
                         asks for exactly this wording; revoked and mangled look the same, on purpose.
     • fresh           — no cookie at all; just the form.

   Failures are indistinguishable by design. Unknown, expired, already-used, and malformed codes all
   produce one sentence, because anything finer turns an anonymous endpoint into an oracle for which
   codes exist (§4.2: "failed attempts burn nothing but the rate budget"). *@

<PageTitle>Pair this display</PageTitle>

@code {
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private bool _wasDisconnected;
    private Guid? _pairedTable;
    private string? _pairedTableLabel;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "display-pair")]
    private PairInputModel PairInput { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds PairInput itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        PairInput ??= new();

        // The middleware has already run, so a live credential is visible as the request's principal and
        // a dead one has already been cleared from the response — but the request's own copy is still
        // readable, which is how "disconnected" is told apart from "never paired" (§11.5).
        _pairedTable = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableIdentifierFor(HttpContext.User);
        _pairedTableLabel = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableLabelFor(HttpContext.User);
        _wasDisconnected = _pairedTable is null && DisplayDeviceCookie.WasPresented(HttpContext.Request);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Redeems the typed code. Normalization (case, spaces, hyphens) happens inside the service, so what
    /// a person read off one screen and typed into another does not have to match byte for byte.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task PairAsync()
    {
        RedeemPairingCodeResult result = await Pairing.RedeemPairingCodeAsync(
            PairInput.Code, PairInput.DeviceLabel, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == RedeemPairingCodeOutcome.Paired
            && result.DeviceIdentifier is { } device
            && result.TableIdentifier is { } table
            && result.DeviceSecret is { } secret)
        {
            // The secret exists in memory exactly once, here: only its SHA-256 hash was stored (§4.2).
            DisplayDeviceCookie.Write(HttpContext.Response, device, secret);
            Navigation.NavigateTo(DisplayRoutes.ForTable(table));
            return;
        }

        // One wording for every refusal. A deactivated table, an expired code, a used code and a typo
        // must be indistinguishable from out here (§4.2).
        _errorMessage = "That code was not recognised. Codes work once and expire quickly — ask for a "
            + "fresh one and try again.";
    }

    private sealed class PairInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the pairing code.")]
        [StringLength(32, MinimumLength = 8, ErrorMessage = "A pairing code is 8 characters.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [StringLength(120, ErrorMessage = "Keep the name under 120 characters.")]
        public string? DeviceLabel { get; set; }
    }
}

   things: a QR that re-renders on the rotation boundary, a party-size chip fed by SittingMemberJoined,
   and a connection state that must never let a frozen code masquerade as a fresh one.

   ANONYMOUS at the endpoint, gated in the component. §11.5 says an unpaired device is *redirected* to
   /display/pair, and [Authorize] cannot produce that: a failed policy challenges the default scheme and
   lands the screen on /sign-in, which is meaningless for a tablet. The device principal itself is
   installed by DisplayDeviceAuthenticationMiddleware and reaches the circuit through the cascading
   authentication state, so the gate below is reading a server-set principal, never anything the browser
   claimed. §3.7's "table claim matches {table}" is a comparison against a route value, which likewise
   belongs in the surface — the same place §3.7 already leaves /table's per-sitting membership check.

   Rotation is continuous and independent of sitting state (§4.3), so the timer runs whether or not the
   table has anyone at it. Deactivating the table stops rendering (§4.1) without unpairing the device.

   /_framework/blazor.web.js cannot be fetched, this page is prerendered HTML and nothing else: the code
   painted at page load stays on the glass indefinitely, looking exactly like a live one. That is why the
   surface publishes data-live (see IsLiveAttributeValue) and why Program.cs asks for the build-time
   static web assets manifest outside Development. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>Which of the §11.5 states this display resolved to.</summary>
    private enum DisplayStage
    {
        /// <summary>No live device credential: §11.5 sends the screen to the pairing surface.</summary>
        NotPaired,

        /// <summary>A live device, but it belongs to a different table (§3.7's table-claim rule).</summary>
        WrongTable,

        /// <summary>Paired and correct, but the table is deactivated — no code renders (§4.1).</summary>
        TableOutOfService,

        /// <summary>Paired, correct, and in service: the rotating QR.</summary>
        Live,
    }

    private DisplayStage _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
    private Guid? _deviceIdentifier;
    private Guid? _deviceTable;
    private string? _deviceTableLabel;
    private string _tableLabel = string.Empty;
    private TableJoinQrCode? _qr;
    private int _partySize;
    private int _refreshSequence;
    private bool _loaded;

    // Captured once, so nothing ever touches _lifetime.Token after Dispose has run.
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _lifetime = new();
    private CancellationToken _stopping;
    private IDisposable? _subscription;
    private bool _liveWorkStarted;
    private bool _disposed;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    private string PageTitleText => _stage == DisplayStage.NotPaired
        ? "Pair this display"
        : string.IsNullOrEmpty(_tableLabel) ? "Table display" : _tableLabel;

    /// <summary>
    /// How long a rendered code stays trustworthy, for js/display.js (§11.5). The arithmetic lives in
    /// <see cref="DisplayRefreshSchedule"/> so it can be tested without a circuit.
    /// </summary>
    private int FreshForMilliseconds
        => DisplayRefreshSchedule.FreshForMilliseconds(Options.TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds);

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether a live circuit produced this markup — <c>"true"</c> only in interactive-server rendering,
    /// <c>"false"</c> during the prerender pass.
    ///
    /// <para>Published because §11.5's central hazard is that <em>a frozen QR looks exactly like a live
    /// one</em>, and the most complete way for it to freeze is for interactivity never to arrive at all:
    /// if <c>/_framework/blazor.web.js</c> cannot be fetched, the prerendered code sits on the glass for
    /// as long as the tablet is left alone, and nothing else on the page differs by so much as a pixel.
    /// One attribute turns that into something an operator can read in dev tools and something the §16.3
    /// scenarios can wait for, instead of a display that simply never advances.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><c>js/display.js</c> does not need it: the staleness curtain already covers a circuit that
    /// dies <em>later</em>, because <c>data-refresh-token</c> stops changing. This covers the case where
    /// it never lived.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string IsLiveAttributeValue => RendererInfo.IsInteractive ? "true" : "false";

    /// <summary>
    /// §11.10's second bit: whether this surface has the thing it exists to show. <c>"true"</c> only
    /// once the component has finished resolving which §11.5 state it is in <em>and</em> a join code came
    /// back from <see cref="ITableJoinTokens"/>.
    ///
    /// <para><b>Why the predicate is not simply <c>_loaded</c>, unlike the other five surfaces.</b>
    /// §11.10 defines the bit as "the surface has everything it renders itself for", and on this screen
    /// that is a QR and nothing else. Both of the branches carrying
    /// <c>id="table-display-surface"</c> are reachable with the component fully resolved: the second one
    /// renders "Preparing the join code…" when <c>DescribeCurrentAsync</c> came back empty, which is
    /// transient rather than fatal and so is deliberately not an error page. A bit that read
    /// <c>true</c> there would be true and useless — it would tell a reader the surface is ready on the
    /// one screen where readiness means a code, and §16.3 scenario 2 would go on to spend sixty seconds
    /// in <c>ReadJoinQrPathAsync</c> failing two steps from the cause.</para>
    ///
    /// <para><b>And why not just <c>_qr is not null</c>.</b> Because that conflates "no code yet" with
    /// "no code came back", and only the second is worth reporting. Keeping <c>_loaded</c> in the
    /// conjunction means the attribute distinguishes a surface still resolving from one that resolved
    /// and got nothing — the first is patience, the second is §4.3 not answering.</para>
    ///
    /// <para>This is the honest reading of the rule rather than an exception to it. The uniform thing
    /// across all six surfaces is the <em>question</em> — has this markup got what a reader came for —
    /// not the expression that answers it. §11.10 says so, and the §16.4 contract test pins the shape
    /// (a property named <c>IsLoadedAttributeValue</c> feeding the attribute) rather than the body, for
    /// exactly this reason.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private string IsLoadedAttributeValue => _loaded && _qr is not null ? "true" : "false";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _stopping = _lifetime.Token;

        if (AuthenticationStateTask is null)
        {
            _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
            _loaded = true;
            return;
        }

        // The cascading authentication state is the circuit-safe way to read the principal: there is no
        // HttpContext once the component is interactive, and it works identically during the prerender
        // pass. The device principal reaches both because the middleware runs on /display AND /_blazor.
        AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;

        _deviceIdentifier = DisplayDevicePrincipal.DeviceIdentifierFor(state.User);
        _deviceTable = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableIdentifierFor(state.User);
        _deviceTableLabel = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableLabelFor(state.User);

        if (_deviceIdentifier is null || _deviceTable is null)
        {
            // §11.5: "Unpaired device → redirect /display/pair". During the prerender pass this becomes
            // an HTTP redirect and the circuit never starts; on the circuit it is a navigation. The
            // rendered not-paired card above stands behind it either way.
            _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
            _loaded = true;
            Navigation.NavigateTo(DisplayRoutes.Pair);
            return;
        }

        if (_deviceTable.Value != TableId)
        {
            _stage = DisplayStage.WrongTable;
            _loaded = true;
            return;
        }

        _tableLabel = _deviceTableLabel ?? string.Empty;
        await LoadAsync();

        // Latched on every path out of this method, including the three early returns above: §11.10's
        // bit means "finished deciding", and an unpaired screen or one on the wrong table has decided.
        // Set before NavigateTo rather than after, because on the prerender pass that call throws a
        // NavigationException the framework swallows and nothing below it would run.
        _loaded = true;

        StartLiveWorkIfNeeded();
    }

    // A safety net, not the primary path: OnInitializedAsync above starts the live work as soon as it knows
    // the stage, which needs no render at all. This catches any future edit that returns early and still
    // ends up in a stage worth refreshing. firstRender is deliberately ignored — see below.
    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
        => StartLiveWorkIfNeeded();

    /// <summary>
    /// Starts the §4.3 refresh timer and the §9 subscription, once, as soon as this component is both
    /// interactive and past the point of knowing which §11.5 state it is in.
    ///
    /// <para><b>Deliberately not gated on <c>firstRender</c>, which is the bug this replaces.</b>
    /// <c>ComponentBase</c> calls <c>StateHasChanged()</c> the moment <c>OnInitializedAsync</c> yields,
    /// and it yields on the first of four database round trips inside <see cref="LoadAsync"/>. The
    /// client's acknowledgement of that first (empty) batch is one loopback message and routinely beats
    /// them, so <c>OnAfterRender(firstRender: true)</c> arrives while <c>_stage</c> is still its default
    /// <c>NotPaired</c> — a state the old guard rejected. <c>firstRender</c> is never true again, so the
    /// refresh loop was never started at all, and the display sat frozen on the code it was born with for
    /// as long as the tablet was left alone. Intermittent by construction: it turns on which of a
    /// WebSocket round trip and four queries finishes first.</para>
    ///
    /// <para>Idempotence comes from <c>_liveWorkStarted</c> rather than from the lifecycle, so it does not
    /// matter how many times or from where this is called. <c>RendererInfo.IsInteractive</c> is what keeps
    /// the prerender pass from starting a timer on a render that is about to be thrown away — the honest
    /// question, and the one <c>firstRender</c> was standing in for.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private void StartLiveWorkIfNeeded()
    {
        if (_liveWorkStarted || _disposed || !RendererInfo.IsInteractive)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Nothing to keep fresh, and nothing that will ever become fresh: an unpaired device is on its way
        // to /display/pair, and a device on the wrong table renders no code by design (§3.7). Not latched,
        // because both are terminal for this component instance — a re-pair is a new page load.
        if (_stage is DisplayStage.NotPaired or DisplayStage.WrongTable)
        {
            return;
        }

        _liveWorkStarted = true;
        _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
        _ = RunRefreshLoopAsync();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Re-reads everything the surface shows. Revalidating the device on every pass is what makes §4.2's
    /// "revocation kills the device on its next request <b>or circuit revalidation</b>" true for a screen
    /// that may sit on one circuit for a week — and it doubles as the <c>last_seen_at</c> heartbeat,
    /// since that touch is rate-limited to once a minute inside the authenticator.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        DisplayDeviceSession? session = await Devices.RevalidateAsync(_deviceIdentifier!.Value, _stopping);
        if (session is null)
        {
            _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
            _qr = null;
            return;
        }

        _tableLabel = session.TableLabel;
        _deviceTableLabel = session.TableLabel;

        if (!session.TableIsActive)
        {
            // §4.1: deactivating a table stops its display rendering. The device stays paired.
            _stage = DisplayStage.TableOutOfService;
            _qr = null;
            return;
        }

        _stage = DisplayStage.Live;
        _qr = await JoinTokens.DescribeCurrentAsync(TableId, _stopping);

        TableSittingSummary? sitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingAsync(TableId, _stopping);
        _partySize = sitting?.MemberCount ?? 0;
        _refreshSequence++;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The window-aligned refresh (§4.3: "the display re-renders on a server timer aligned to the window
    /// boundary — fire at <c>(window_index+1) × rotation</c>"). The next boundary comes from the code
    /// just rendered, so the loop stays aligned without keeping its own notion of the window.
    ///
    /// <para><b>Why the broad catch.</b> This loop is fire-and-forget, so an exception escaping it becomes
    /// an unobserved task exception: the loop stops, nothing is logged, and the screen keeps showing the
    /// last code it managed to render — forever, and identically to a healthy one. A dropped connection or
    /// a moment of database unavailability, neither of them the display's fault, would permanently freeze a
    /// screen the restaurant is trusting. Absorbing it and waiting for the next boundary is the behaviour
    /// §11.5 actually wants, and it is not a swallow: it is logged, and <c>_refreshSequence</c> stops
    /// advancing, so <c>js/display.js</c> raises the offline curtain if the trouble outlasts
    /// <c>data-fresh-for-ms</c>. Cancellation and disposal still end the loop, because those mean the
    /// circuit is genuinely gone.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private async Task RunRefreshLoopAsync()
    {
        while (!_stopping.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            try
            {
                await Task.Delay(DelayUntilNextWindow(), _stopping);
                await InvokeAsync(RefreshAsync);
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                return; // the circuit went away
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                return; // torn down mid-flight
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                Logger.LogWarning(
                    exception,
                    "Refreshing the display surface for table {TableIdentifier} failed; retrying at the next rotation boundary.",
                    TableId);
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task RefreshAsync()
    {
        await LoadAsync();

        if (_stage == DisplayStage.NotPaired)
        {
            // Revoked while we were watching. A full-page navigation re-runs the middleware, which
            // clears the dead cookie, so the pairing screen greets it with "this display was
            // disconnected" rather than a bare form (§11.5).
            Navigation.NavigateTo(DisplayRoutes.Pair, forceLoad: true);
            return;
        }

        StateHasChanged();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Time until just after the next rotation boundary, taken from the code currently on screen so the
    /// loop stays aligned without keeping its own notion of the window. The arithmetic — the overshoot,
    /// the floor, and the ceiling that defends against a clock jump — lives in
    /// <see cref="DisplayRefreshSchedule"/>, where it is unit-tested.
    /// </summary>
    private TimeSpan DelayUntilNextWindow()
        => DisplayRefreshSchedule.DelayUntilNextRefresh(
            Clock.UtcNow,
            _qr?.NextRotationAt,
            Options.TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds);

    /// <summary>
    /// §9 attaches the party-size chip to <c>SittingMemberJoined</c>, and a close empties the table, so
    /// both are re-read. The sitting identifier is deliberately not compared: the very notification that
    /// matters most — the first person joining — announces a sitting this surface has never seen, so
    /// filtering on a known id would drop it. One cheap scoped query per table event is the right trade.
    /// </summary>
    private void OnDomainNotification(DomainNotification notification)
    {
        if (notification is not SittingMemberJoined && notification is not SittingClosed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _ = InvokeAsync(async () =>
        {
            try
            {
                TableSittingSummary? sitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingAsync(TableId, _stopping);
                _partySize = sitting?.MemberCount ?? 0;
                StateHasChanged();
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Disposed between the broadcast and the query; nothing to update.
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                // Same, one layer down.
            }
        });
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _disposed = true;
        _subscription?.Dispose();
        _lifetime.Cancel();
        _lifetime.Dispose();
    }
}

    private bool _needsSetup;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // Point a fresh deployment at /setup while no administrator exists (§3.6). Best-effort: the

@* The kitchen board (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §10, §11.2).

   Interactive server, prerendered, and the only surface in the tree that is expected to sit on one
   circuit for a whole service. Everything it shows is derived: the queue is the kitchen_pending_line
   view (§8.3), the Undo list is IKitchenBoardReads, the "86" panel is the menu. It holds no state of its
   own except the alert state, which is a browser-audio permission and therefore cannot be anything but
   circuit state (§10.3).

   Nothing here enforces §6.5. Every tap goes through IOrderWorkflow to the one transaction, which
   re-decides under the lock (§6.6) — so two cooks tapping the same line at the same moment produce one
   fulfillment and one refusal, and the refusal is shown rather than swallowed. What this surface
   refuses on its own it refuses only to make the answer immediate.

   The actor role is read from the principal rather than assumed: §6.2 lets kitchen OR administrator
   author a fulfillment, and an administrator covering the pass must not be recorded as the kitchen. *@
